name.zh: 霍普韦尔仪式性土方工程

summary.en: Across the Ohio valley, communities of the Hopewell tradition raised vast geometric enclosures of earth (circles, squares and octagons) aligned with the cycles of the moon, and exchanged obsidian, copper, mica and shell across half the continent.
summary.zh: 在俄亥俄河谷，霍普韦尔传统的社群用泥土筑起巨大的几何形围垣（圆形、方形和八角形），其朝向与月亮周期相合；他们还在半个大陆范围内交换黑曜石、铜、云母和贝壳。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks
Britannica: Hopewell culture
Bradley T. Lepper, Ohio Archaeology (2005)

note: Construction spans roughly 1–400 CE; individual sites are dated by radiocarbon only approximately.

story.en:
Between about the first and fifth centuries CE, people in southern Ohio built some of the largest geometric earthworks ever made. At Newark a circle joined to an octagon covers some fifty hectares, and its walls point to the northernmost rise of the moon in its 18.6-year cycle, an alignment that implies generations of patient sky-watching.

The Hopewell were not an empire but a web of farming and foraging communities linked by ceremony. Into their burial mounds went obsidian from the Yellowstone region, copper from Lake Superior, mica from the southern Appalachians and shells from the Gulf of Mexico, worked into hands, birds and serpents of startling skill.

The exchange network faded after about 400, and later farmers mostly ignored the old enclosures. Many were ploughed away in the 19th century; the octagon at Newark survived partly because it became a golf course. In 2023 eight of the sites were inscribed together on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
story.zh:
大约在公元1至5世纪，俄亥俄南部的人们修建了史上规模最大的一批几何形土方工程。纽瓦克的圆形与八角形围垣相连，占地约五十公顷，其墙体指向月亮在18.6年周期中最北的升起点，这意味着数代人耐心的观天积累。

霍普韦尔并非一个帝国，而是由仪式联结起来的农耕与采集社群网络。他们的墓冢中有来自黄石一带的黑曜石、苏必利尔湖的铜、阿巴拉契亚山南部的云母和墨西哥湾的贝壳，被精巧地制成手掌、飞鸟和蛇形。

约400年后，这一交换网络逐渐衰落，后来的农人大多不再使用这些围垣。许多遗址在19世纪被犁平；纽瓦克八角形围垣之所以部分幸存，是因为它成了一座高尔夫球场。2023年，其中八处遗址作为整体被列入联合国教科文组织《世界遗产名录》。

summary.en: In the Sonoran Desert around present-day Phoenix, Hohokam farmers dug hundreds of kilometres of irrigation canals from the Salt and Gila rivers, sustaining villages with ball courts and platform mounds until the system broke down in the 15th century.
summary.zh: 在今菲尼克斯周围的索诺兰沙漠，霍霍坎农人从索尔特河和希拉河引水，开凿了数百公里的灌溉渠，养活了拥有球场和平台土丘的村落，直到15世纪这一体系崩溃。

sources.title: Britannica: Hohokam culture
Suzanne K. Fish & Paul R. Fish (eds.), The Hohokam Millennium (2008)
S'edav Va'aki Museum (Pueblo Grande), City of Phoenix

note: Hohokam culture is usually dated c. 300–1450; large canal systems in the Salt River valley grew from about the 7th century.

story.en:
Long before modern Phoenix, the lower Salt River valley held one of the largest irrigation systems in the pre-Columbian Americas. Using digging sticks and baskets, Hohokam communities cut main canals up to twenty metres wide and fed a branching web of laterals that watered maize, beans, squash, cotton and agave in a land with less than 200 millimetres of rain a year.

The canals demanded cooperation: villages sharing a headgate had to clean silt, repair breaches after floods and divide water fairly. Ball courts resembling Mesoamerican ones, and later platform mounds, suggest how that cooperation was organised.

After a run of catastrophic floods and droughts in the 14th century, the system frayed and the large settlements emptied by about 1450. The O'odham peoples regard the Hohokam (Huhugam) as ancestors, and early Anglo settlers of Phoenix reopened some of the old channels; modern canals still follow their lines.
story.zh:
早在现代菲尼克斯出现之前，索尔特河下游河谷就拥有前哥伦布时代美洲规模最大的灌溉体系之一。霍霍坎社群用掘土棒和篮筐开凿出宽达二十米的干渠，再分出纵横交错的支渠，在年降水不足200毫米的土地上浇灌玉米、豆类、南瓜、棉花和龙舌兰。

运河需要协作：共用一个渠首的村落必须清淤、在洪水后修补决口，并公平分水。类似中美洲的球场以及后来的平台土丘，透露出这种协作的组织方式。

14世纪接连发生的特大洪水和干旱使这一体系瓦解，大型聚落约在1450年前后人去楼空。奥哈姆人视霍霍坎（Huhugam）为祖先；菲尼克斯早期的英裔移民曾重新疏通部分古渠，今天的运河仍沿着它们的走向。

summary.en: Ancestral Puebloans built multistorey "great houses" such as Pueblo Bonito in Chaco Canyon, New Mexico, linked by straight roads to outlying communities. Chaco was the ceremonial and trading centre of the Four Corners region until a long drought after 1130.
summary.zh: 先民普韦布洛人在新墨西哥州查科峡谷修建了博尼托镇等多层“大房子”，并以笔直的道路连接周边社群。查科一直是四角地区的仪式与贸易中心，直到1130年后长期干旱来临。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Chaco Culture
Britannica: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
Stephen H. Lekson, The Chaco Meridian (2nd ed., 2015)

note: Construction at Pueblo Bonito began in the mid-800s; the major building phase ran c. 1030–1130 (tree-ring dates).

story.en:
Chaco Canyon is a dry, shallow gash in northwestern New Mexico, yet between the 9th and 12th centuries it held a dozen planned buildings of a size not matched in North America until the 1800s. Pueblo Bonito, the largest, rose four or five storeys and contained some 650 rooms and dozens of round ceremonial kivas. Its builders carried more than 200,000 pine and fir beams from mountains up to 80 kilometres away.

Few people seem to have lived in the great houses year-round. Archaeologists read them as stages for pilgrimage and feasting: dug-out roads run arrow-straight across the desert, and Pueblo Bonito yielded cacao residue in cylinder jars and scarlet macaw skeletons, both traded from Mesoamerica.

A severe drought after 1130 ended new building. Chacoan people dispersed to places such as Aztec and Mesa Verde, and today's Pueblo nations of New Mexico and Arizona remember Chaco as an ancestral home.
story.zh:
查科峡谷是新墨西哥州西北部一道干燥的浅谷，但在9至12世纪间，这里矗立着十多座规划宏大的建筑，其规模直到19世纪才在北美被超越。最大的博尼托镇高四五层，约有650个房间和数十座圆形仪式厅“基瓦”。建造者从远达80公里外的山地运来了二十多万根松木和冷杉梁。

“大房子”里常年居住的人似乎不多。考古学家认为它们是朝圣与宴飨的舞台：开凿出的道路笔直地穿越荒漠；博尼托镇的圆筒罐中发现了可可残留，还出土了绯红金刚鹦鹉的骨骼，二者都来自中美洲的贸易。

1130年后的一场严重干旱终结了新的营建。查科人散居到阿兹特克遗址、梅萨维德等地；今天新墨西哥和亚利桑那的普韦布洛诸民族仍把查科视为祖居之地。

summary.en: Around 1050 a town near present-day St. Louis was rapidly rebuilt around a vast plaza and Monks Mound, the largest earthen pyramid north of Mexico. At its height Cahokia held perhaps 10,000–20,000 people, the largest city in what is now the United States before the 1780s.
summary.zh: 约1050年，今圣路易斯附近的一座城镇围绕巨大的广场和墨西哥以北最大的土台金字塔“僧侣丘”迅速重建。卡霍基亚鼎盛时人口或达一至两万，是18世纪80年代之前今美国境内最大的城市。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site
Britannica: Cahokia Mounds
Timothy R. Pauketat, Cahokia: Ancient America's Great City on the Mississippi (2009)

note: Population estimates range widely (c. 8,000–40,000 including suburbs); the 1050 "Big Bang" date follows Pauketat.

story.en:
In the middle of the 11th century, something dramatic happened in the American Bottom, the floodplain opposite modern St. Louis. Within a generation the scattered village there was levelled and rebuilt to a plan: a twenty-hectare Grand Plaza, more than a hundred earthen mounds and, at the centre, Monks Mound, whose base covers more ground than the Great Pyramid of Giza. Archaeologist Timothy Pauketat calls it Cahokia's "Big Bang".

Cahokia's religion and pottery styles spread along the Mississippi and its tributaries, seeding the Mississippian world. Its leaders staged great feasts and games of chunkey, and in Mound 72 were buried a high-status man on a bed of shell beads together with dozens of sacrificed young women.

By 1200 Cahokia was shrinking, a log palisade now ringing its centre, and by about 1350 it was largely abandoned, perhaps through flooding, drought and political strife. The name Cahokia comes from an Illinois people who lived nearby centuries later.
story.zh:
11世纪中叶，今圣路易斯对岸的密西西比河泛滥平原“美洲谷地”发生了剧变。不到一代人的时间，这里分散的村落被夷平，并按规划重建：二十公顷的大广场、一百多座土丘，中央则是僧侣丘，其底面积超过吉萨大金字塔。考古学家蒂莫西·波克塔特称之为卡霍基亚的“大爆炸”。

卡霍基亚的宗教和陶器风格沿密西西比河及其支流传播，孕育了整个密西西比文化世界。其首领举办盛大的宴会和“昌基”滚石游戏；72号丘中葬有一名地位很高的男子，身下铺满贝珠，同葬的还有数十名被献祭的年轻女子。

到1200年，卡霍基亚开始萎缩，中心区修起了木栅；约1350年，这里大体被废弃，原因可能是洪水、干旱和政治纷争。“卡霍基亚”之名来自几个世纪后住在附近的伊利诺伊部族。

name.zh: 红发埃里克殖民格陵兰

summary.en: Outlawed from Iceland, Erik the Red explored southwest Greenland and around 985 returned with a fleet of settlers, founding his farm at Brattahlíð. The Norse colony grew to perhaps 2,000–3,000 people in the Eastern and Western Settlements.
summary.zh: 红发埃里克被冰岛放逐后考察了格陵兰西南部，约985年率船队带移民返回，在布拉塔利德建立农庄。诺斯殖民地在东、西两处定居点发展到约两三千人。

sources.title: Britannica: Erik the Red
UNESCO World Heritage: Kujataa Greenland: Norse and Inuit Farming at the Edge of the Ice Cap
Eiríks saga rauða (Saga of Erik the Red) and Grænlendinga saga

note: The sagas place the settlement voyage c. 985/986; Íslendingabók dates it 14 or 15 winters before Iceland's conversion (c. 999/1000).

story.en:
According to the Icelandic sagas, Erik Thorvaldsson, called the Red, was a man who killed easily: driven from Norway with his father after a feud, he was then outlawed from Iceland for three years after more killings. He used his exile to sail west to a land glimpsed decades earlier and spent three summers exploring its fjords.

Returning to Iceland, he gave the place an inviting name. The sagas say he called it Greenland because people would be more eager to go to a land with a good name. Around 985, some 25 ships set out with settlers and livestock; only fourteen are said to have arrived.

Erik built his farm at Brattahlíð at the head of a sheltered fjord, where his wife Thjodhild is said to have built a small church after their son Leif brought Christianity. The colony he founded would last more than four centuries.
story.zh:
据冰岛萨迦记载，红发埃里克·托瓦尔德松动辄杀人：他先随父亲因仇杀被逐出挪威，后又因再次杀人被冰岛判处三年放逐。他利用流放期间向西航行，前往数十年前有人瞥见过的一片陆地，花了三个夏天探察那里的峡湾。

回到冰岛后，他给那里起了一个诱人的名字。萨迦说，他称之为“格陵兰”（绿色的土地），因为好名字能吸引更多人前往。约985年，约25艘船载着移民和牲畜出发，据说只有14艘抵达。

埃里克在一处避风峡湾深处的布拉塔利德建起农庄；据说在儿子莱夫带回基督教后，他的妻子肖德希尔德在那里修建了一座小教堂。他所开创的殖民地延续了四个多世纪。

name.zh: 诺斯人抵达兰塞奥兹牧草地

summary.en: At the northern tip of Newfoundland, Norse voyagers from Greenland built a small base of turf halls and a smithy around 1000. Tree rings in wood they cut show activity in 1021, the earliest securely dated European presence in the Americas.
summary.zh: 在纽芬兰岛北端，来自格陵兰的诺斯航海者约在1000年建起了由草皮长屋和铁匠铺组成的小型据点。他们砍伐的木材年轮显示1021年有人在此活动，这是欧洲人在美洲最早有确切年代的存在。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: L'Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site
Kuitems et al., "Evidence for European presence in the Americas in AD 1021", Nature 601 (2022)
Britannica: L'Anse aux Meadows

story.en:
Two Icelandic sagas tell of voyages from Greenland to lands in the west called Helluland, Markland and Vinland, led by Leif Erikson and others around the year 1000. For centuries scholars argued over whether these were real. In 1960 the Norwegian explorer Helge Ingstad and the archaeologist Anne Stine Ingstad, guided by a local man, George Decker, found low grassy ridges at L'Anse aux Meadows that proved to be the remains of eight Norse buildings.

The site was a short-lived gateway, not a colony: halls for perhaps a hundred people, a forge for making boat rivets, and butternuts that grow only far to the south, hinting at trips deeper into the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

In 2021 researchers found the sharp marks of metal blades on wood from the site and matched its tree rings to a spike in atmospheric radiocarbon caused by a solar storm in 993. The felling year was 1021, exactly a thousand years before the study.
story.zh:
两部冰岛萨迦讲述了约1000年莱夫·埃里克松等人从格陵兰向西航行，到达名为赫尔陆兰、马克陆兰和文兰的土地。几个世纪以来，学者们一直争论这些故事是否属实。1960年，挪威探险家黑尔格·英斯塔和考古学家安妮·斯泰恩·英斯塔在当地人乔治·德克的指引下，在兰塞奥兹牧草地发现了一些长满青草的低矮土垄，后来证实是八座诺斯建筑的遗迹。

这里只是一个短暂使用的中转站，而非殖民地：长屋可容纳约百人，有一座锻造船钉的铁匠铺，还出土了只生长在遥远南方的灰胡桃，暗示他们曾深入圣劳伦斯湾。

2021年，研究人员在遗址出土的木材上找到金属刃具留下的切痕，并把其年轮与993年一次太阳风暴造成的大气放射性碳峰值相对应，测得伐木年份为1021年，恰在研究发表前整整一千年。

name.zh: 图勒人横越北极的迁徙

summary.en: Ancestors of the Inuit, the Thule people, spread from northern Alaska across the Canadian Arctic to Greenland within perhaps a few generations in the 13th century, hunting bowhead whales from skin boats and replacing the older Dorset (Tuniit) population.
summary.zh: 因纽特人的祖先图勒人在13世纪或许只用了几代人的时间，就从阿拉斯加北部横越加拿大北极地区抵达格陵兰。他们驾皮船猎捕弓头鲸，并取代了更早的多塞特人（图尼特人）。

label.zh: 阿拉斯加北部的比尔尼克故地
麦肯齐河三角洲沿岸
维多利亚岛与科罗内申湾
康沃利斯岛与兰开斯特海峡
史密斯海峡
格陵兰西北部（图勒地区）

sources.title: Britannica: Thule culture
T. Max Friesen & Charles D. Arnold, "The Timing of the Thule Migration", American Antiquity 73 (2008)
Raghavan et al., "The genetic prehistory of the New World Arctic", Science 345 (2014)

note: Older models placed the migration c. 1000; refined radiocarbon dating since 2000 favours a rapid move in the 13th century.

story.en:
Around the 13th century, people from the coasts of northern Alaska began one of the fastest long-distance migrations in human history. Within a few generations their descendants were living 4,000 kilometres to the east, in Greenland. Archaeologists call them the Thule culture, after a site in northwest Greenland; they are the direct ancestors of today's Inuit.

They travelled with remarkable equipment: large open skin boats (umiat) and kayaks, toggling harpoons and floats for taking bowhead whales, dog sleds, and snow houses. Why they moved so fast is debated, perhaps to follow whales, perhaps drawn by meteoritic iron in Greenland and by contact with Norse traders.

The Arctic was not empty. The Dorset people, called Tuniit in Inuit oral history, had lived there for centuries; within about a century of Thule arrival they vanished, and genetic studies show little intermixing. In Greenland the newcomers met the Norse, who called them skrælings.
story.zh:
约13世纪，来自阿拉斯加北部沿海的人群开始了人类历史上最迅速的长途迁徙之一。只用了几代人，他们的后代就已生活在4000公里以东的格陵兰。考古学家以格陵兰西北部的一处遗址将其命名为“图勒文化”，他们是今天因纽特人的直系祖先。

他们拥有出色的装备：大型敞篷皮船（乌米亚克）和皮划艇、用于猎捕弓头鲸的转向式鱼叉与浮囊、狗拉雪橇以及雪屋。他们为何迁徙得如此之快仍有争论：或许是追随鲸群，或许是被格陵兰的陨铁和与诺斯商人的接触所吸引。

北极并非无人之地。多塞特人（因纽特口述历史中的“图尼特人”）已在那里生活了数百年；图勒人到来后约一个世纪内，他们便消失了，遗传学研究显示两者几乎没有混血。在格陵兰，新来者遇到了诺斯人，后者称他们为“斯克雷林人”。

summary.en: In the late 12th and 13th centuries Ancestral Puebloans on Mesa Verde, Colorado, moved into stone villages built in canyon alcoves, such as Cliff Palace with about 150 rooms. By about 1285, amid the Great Drought and conflict, the whole region was abandoned.
summary.zh: 12世纪末至13世纪，科罗拉多州梅萨维德的先民普韦布洛人迁入建在峡谷岩洞里的石砌村落，如约有150个房间的悬崖宫。约到1285年，在大旱和冲突中，整个地区被弃置。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Mesa Verde National Park
Britannica: Mesa Verde National Park
National Park Service: Cliff Palace

note: Tree-ring dates put most cliff-dwelling construction between c. 1190 and 1260; the last dated timbers are from the late 1270s.

story.en:
For six centuries farmers had lived on top of Mesa Verde in pit houses and then masonry pueblos. Then, around 1200, many families moved down into the shallow caves of the canyon walls, building tower-like rooms, granaries and kivas tucked under overhangs that could be reached only by handholds and ladders.

Tree-ring dating shows most of these cliff dwellings were built in just a few generations, and the last beams were cut in the late 1270s. The years 1276–1299 were a severe drought; skeletal evidence of violence and burned villages across the Mesa Verde region point to a society under great stress.

By about 1285 tens of thousands of people had left the region, migrating south to the Rio Grande and the Hopi and Zuni lands, where their descendants still live. In 1888 two ranchers searching for stray cattle saw Cliff Palace across the canyon; Mesa Verde became a national park in 1906.
story.zh:
六个世纪以来，农人们一直生活在梅萨维德台地顶部，先住半地穴房屋，后住石砌村落。约1200年起，许多家庭迁到峡谷崖壁的浅洞中，在悬岩下修建塔状房间、粮仓和基瓦，只能借助岩壁上的抓手和梯子出入。

树轮测年显示，这些悬崖居所大多在短短几代人内建成，最后一批梁木伐于13世纪70年代末。1276至1299年是一场严重干旱；整个梅萨维德地区的骸骨暴力痕迹和焚毁的村落显示，当时社会承受着巨大压力。

约到1285年，数以万计的人离开了这一地区，南迁至格兰德河流域以及霍皮和祖尼人的土地，他们的后代至今仍生活在那里。1888年，两名寻找走失牛群的牧场主隔着峡谷望见了悬崖宫；1906年，梅萨维德被辟为国家公园。

summary.en: Through the Great Law of Peace (Gayanashagowa), the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca nations formed a confederacy governed by a council of fifty hereditary chiefs chosen by clan mothers. Its founding is credited to the Peacemaker and Hiawatha.
summary.zh: 通过《和平大法》，莫霍克、奥奈达、奥农达加、卡尤加和塞内卡五个民族结成联盟，由氏族母亲推选的五十位世袭酋长组成的议事会治理。联盟的创立归功于“和平使者”与海华沙。

sources.title: Britannica: Iroquois Confederacy
Haudenosaunee Confederacy (official site): Who we are
Dean R. Snow, The Iroquois (1994)

note: The founding date is debated: oral tradition and an eclipse argument point to 1142 (Mann & Fields 1997); most archaeologists favour c. 1450–1525. 1450 is used as a conventional date.

story.en:
According to Haudenosaunee tradition, the nations south of Lake Ontario were once locked in cycles of revenge killing. A Huron-born prophet, remembered as the Peacemaker, crossed the lake in a canoe of white stone carrying a message of peace, power and righteousness. He found an ally in Hiawatha, an Onondaga or Mohawk man grieving the deaths of his daughters, and the Peacemaker consoled him with strings of shell beads, the origin of the condolence ceremony and of wampum.

Together they persuaded the Mohawk, Oneida, Cayuga and Seneca. The last to agree was the fearsome Onondaga chief Tadodaho, whose hair, the story says, writhed with snakes; when it was combed straight, Onondaga became the fire-keeper of the league. The weapons of war were buried beneath a white pine.

The resulting Great Law created a council of fifty chiefs, nominated and removable by clan mothers. The Tuscarora joined around 1722, making the Six Nations.
story.zh:
据豪德诺索尼传说，安大略湖以南的各民族曾陷于冤冤相报的仇杀循环。一位出生于休伦人中的先知，即人们记忆中的“和平使者”，乘一艘白石独木舟渡湖而来，带来和平、力量与正义的讯息。他找到了盟友海华沙，一位因女儿们相继死去而悲痛欲绝的奥农达加（或莫霍克）男子；和平使者用贝珠串抚慰他，这便是吊唁仪式和贝壳串珠“万普姆”的由来。

两人一同说服了莫霍克、奥奈达、卡尤加和塞内卡人。最后一个同意的是令人畏惧的奥农达加酋长塔多达霍，传说他的头发是一团扭动的蛇；当头发被梳直后，奥农达加成为联盟的“守火者”。战争的武器被埋在一棵白松之下。

由此诞生的《和平大法》设立了五十位酋长组成的议事会，酋长由氏族母亲提名并可被其罢免。约1722年塔斯卡洛拉人加入，形成“六族联盟”。

summary.en: The last written record from Norse Greenland is a wedding at Hvalsey church in September 1408. Within a few decades the Eastern Settlement was empty, after cooling climate, the collapse of the walrus-ivory trade and isolation from Norway.
summary.zh: 诺斯格陵兰最后的文字记录是1408年9月在赫瓦尔塞教堂举行的一场婚礼。此后数十年间，随着气候变冷、海象牙贸易崩溃以及与挪威的联系中断，东定居点人去楼空。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Kujataa Greenland
Jette Arneborg, "Norse Greenland: Reflections on Settlement and Depopulation", in Contact, Continuity and Collapse (2003)
Barrett et al., "Walrus ivory trade in the Viking Age and Middle Ages", Proc. Royal Society B 287 (2020)

note: The Western Settlement was abandoned c. 1350; the end of the Eastern Settlement is dated by archaeology to the mid-15th century.

story.en:
In September 1408 Thorstein Olafsson and Sigrid Bjornsdottir, Icelanders whose ship had been driven to Greenland, were married in the stone church at Hvalsey. Letters they later carried home to Iceland are the last written word from Norse Greenland. After that the colony simply fades from the record.

Its decline had been long. The Western Settlement was found deserted around 1350. Europe's appetite for walrus ivory, Greenland's main export, fell as African elephant ivory became available; the Little Ice Age shortened summers and choked the fjords with sea ice; ships from Norway came rarely after the Black Death.

The settlers were not simply stubborn Europeans who refused to adapt, as was once claimed: bone chemistry shows they ate more and more seal. But a farming society of a few thousand people at the edge of the world had little margin. When an expedition from Denmark–Norway arrived in 1721 to look for them, it found only ruins and Inuit.
story.zh:
1408年9月，因船只被风吹到格陵兰的冰岛人托尔斯坦·奥拉夫松和西格丽德·比约恩斯多蒂尔在赫瓦尔塞的石砌教堂成婚。他们后来带回冰岛的书信，是诺斯格陵兰留下的最后文字。此后，这个殖民地就从记载中悄然消失了。

衰落早已开始。约1350年，西定居点被发现已无人烟。随着非洲象牙进入市场，欧洲对格陵兰主要出口品海象牙的需求下降；小冰期缩短了夏季，海冰堵塞了峡湾；黑死病之后，从挪威来的船只越来越少。

定居者并不像过去所说的那样是拒绝适应的顽固欧洲人：骨骼化学分析显示，他们吃的海豹越来越多。但一个只有几千人、位于世界边缘的农业社会回旋余地极小。1721年丹麦—挪威派出探险队寻找他们时，只看到了废墟和因纽特人。

summary.en: Francisco Vázquez de Coronado led some 350 Spaniards and well over a thousand Indigenous Mexican allies north in search of the fabled Seven Cities of Cíbola. They found Zuni and Rio Grande pueblos, saw the Grand Canyon and crossed the Plains to Kansas, but no gold.
summary.zh: 弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多率约350名西班牙人和一千多名墨西哥原住民盟友北上，寻找传说中的“西博拉七城”。他们找到了祖尼人和格兰德河的普韦布洛村落，看到了大峡谷，并穿越大平原直抵堪萨斯，却没有找到黄金。

label.zh: 从新加利西亚的孔波斯特拉出发
攻占祖尼人城镇哈威库（“西博拉”）

label.en: A detachment reaches the Grand Canyon
label.zh: 一支分队抵达大峡谷

label.en: Winter at Tiguex; war with the Tiwa pueblos
label.zh: 在蒂瓜克斯过冬，与蒂瓦人普韦布洛交战
穿越埃斯塔卡多平原
基维拉（堪萨斯的威奇托村落）
返回墨西哥城

sources.title: Britannica: Francisco Vázquez de Coronado
Richard Flint & Shirley Cushing Flint, A Most Splendid Company: The Coronado Expedition in Global Perspective (2019)
National Park Service: Coronado National Memorial

story.en:
The expedition was born of a rumour. A friar, Marcos de Niza, reported in 1539 that he had glimpsed a city larger than Mexico City in the north. The viceroy of New Spain chose the young governor Francisco Vázquez de Coronado to lead a great company, financed partly by his wife's fortune.

Cíbola turned out to be Hawikuh, a Zuni town of stone and adobe, which Coronado stormed in July 1540; he wrote bitterly that the friar had told the truth about nothing. Detachments went west and saw the Grand Canyon, which they could not descend. Over the winter at Tiguex on the Rio Grande the Spaniards seized food and clothing and burned pueblos, opening a long legacy of mistrust.

A Plains captive the Spaniards called the Turk then promised a rich land, Quivira. Coronado rode across a sea of grass and buffalo to central Kansas, found Wichita villages of grass houses, and had the Turk executed. He went home in 1542 discredited; the lands he had crossed were left alone by Spain for half a century.
story.zh:
这次远征源于一则传言。1539年，修士马科斯·德·尼萨报告说，他在北方望见了一座比墨西哥城还大的城市。新西班牙总督选中年轻的省长弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多率领庞大的队伍，部分经费来自他妻子的财产。

所谓西博拉原来是祖尼人用石头和土坯筑成的城镇哈威库，科罗纳多在1540年7月攻下了它，并愤愤地写道修士所说没有一句是真的。分队向西看到了大峡谷，却无法下到谷底。在格兰德河畔的蒂瓜克斯过冬时，西班牙人强征粮食和衣物、焚烧村落，埋下了长期互不信任的种子。

一个被西班牙人称为“土耳其人”的平原俘虏又许诺说有一片富饶之地“基维拉”。科罗纳多穿过野牛成群的茫茫草原来到堪萨斯中部，只找到威奇托人的草屋村落，于是处死了那名向导。1542年他声名扫地地回国；此后半个世纪，西班牙再未踏足他穿越过的土地。

summary.en: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés landed on the Florida coast on 8 September 1565 and founded San Agustín, now the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States. Days later he destroyed the French Huguenot colony at Fort Caroline.
summary.zh: 1565年9月8日，佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯在佛罗里达海岸登陆，建立圣奥古斯丁，这是美国本土至今有人连续居住的最古老的欧洲人所建城市。数日后，他摧毁了法国胡格诺派在卡罗琳堡的殖民地。

sources.title: Britannica: St. Augustine
National Park Service: Castillo de San Marcos, History
Eugene Lyon, The Enterprise of Florida: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés and the Spanish Conquest of 1565–1568 (1976)

story.en:
In 1564 French Protestants built Fort Caroline near the mouth of the St. Johns River, a threat to the Spanish treasure fleets that sailed home along the Florida coast. Philip II sent his best admiral, Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, to remove them. On 8 September 1565, the feast of the Nativity of Mary, Menéndez came ashore at a Timucua village called Seloy, a chaplain celebrated Mass, and the settlement was named for St. Augustine, on whose feast day the coast had been sighted.

A hurricane then wrecked the French fleet sent against him. Menéndez marched overland through the storm, took Fort Caroline, and at an inlet south of his town executed most of the shipwrecked Frenchmen who surrendered; the place is still called Matanzas, "slaughters".

St. Augustine survived pirate raids, English sieges and the transfer of Florida to Britain and back. Its stone fort, the Castillo de San Marcos, built of coquina shell-rock from 1672, still stands.
story.zh:
1564年，法国新教徒在圣约翰斯河口附近修建了卡罗琳堡，威胁到沿佛罗里达海岸返航的西班牙运宝船队。腓力二世派出最得力的海军将领佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯前去清除他们。1565年9月8日，即圣母诞辰节，梅嫩德斯在帖木夸人名为塞洛伊的村落登陆，随军神父主持了弥撒；因船队在圣奥古斯丁节那天望见海岸，定居点便以他命名。

随后一场飓风摧毁了派来攻打他的法国舰队。梅嫩德斯冒着风暴从陆路行军，攻下卡罗琳堡，又在城南的一处海湾处决了大部分投降的法国落难者；那里至今仍叫马坦萨斯，意为“屠杀”。

圣奥古斯丁历经海盗袭击、英国人的围攻，以及佛罗里达几度易手英国又归还西班牙。1672年起用贝壳石灰岩修建的圣马科斯城堡至今犹存。

name.zh: 罗阿诺克“失落的殖民地”

summary.en: Sponsored by Walter Raleigh, English colonists settled on Roanoke Island in present North Carolina in 1585 and again in 1587. When a relief ship finally returned in 1590 the 1587 settlers had vanished, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved on a post.
summary.zh: 在沃尔特·雷利资助下，英国殖民者于1585年和1587年两度在今北卡罗来纳的罗阿诺克岛定居。1590年补给船终于返回时，1587年的移民已不知所踪，只在一根木柱上刻着“CROATOAN”一词。

sources.title: Britannica: Roanoke Island
National Park Service: Fort Raleigh National Historic Site
Karen Ordahl Kupperman, Roanoke: The Abandoned Colony (2nd ed., 2007)

story.en:
England's first attempts at an American colony were made on a low island behind the Outer Banks. A military outpost of 1585 failed within a year, but it left a remarkable record: the scientist Thomas Harriot described the land and its Algonquian peoples, and the painter John White drew their towns, fishing weirs and dances.

In 1587 White returned as governor with about 115 men, women and children. His granddaughter Virginia Dare, born that August, was the first English child born in the Americas. White sailed home for supplies, but the war with Spain and the Armada kept him in England for three years.

When he landed again in August 1590, the houses had been taken down and the settlers were gone. Carved on a palisade post was CROATOAN, the name of an island and people to the south, but storms forced his ship away before he could look. What happened to the colonists remains unknown; archaeologists continue to test theories that they joined nearby Native communities.
story.zh:
英格兰在美洲建立殖民地的最初尝试，是在外滩群岛后面的一座低平岛屿上进行的。1585年的军事前哨不到一年便宣告失败，却留下了珍贵的记录：科学家托马斯·哈里奥特描述了这片土地及其阿尔冈昆诸民族，画家约翰·怀特描绘了他们的村落、鱼梁和舞蹈。

1587年，怀特以总督身份带着约115名男女老幼重返。他的外孙女弗吉尼娅·戴尔于当年8月出生，是第一个在美洲出生的英格兰孩子。怀特回国筹措补给，但对西班牙的战争和无敌舰队把他困在英格兰整整三年。

1590年8月他再次登岛时，房屋已被拆除，移民们无影无踪。栅栏柱上刻着“CROATOAN”，那是南面一座岛屿和一个部族的名字，但风暴迫使他的船驶离，未能前往查找。殖民者的下落至今成谜；考古学家仍在检验他们投奔附近原住民社群的种种假说。

summary.en: Colonists of the Virginia Company landed on a peninsula in the James River on 14 May 1607, founding the first permanent English settlement in North America inside the Powhatan paramount chiefdom. Disease, hunger and war killed most early settlers before tobacco made the colony profitable.
summary.zh: 1607年5月14日，弗吉尼亚公司的殖民者在詹姆斯河上的一个半岛登陆，于波瓦坦大酋邦境内建立了英国在北美的第一个永久定居点。疾病、饥荒和战争夺去了大多数早期移民的生命，后来烟草才使殖民地有利可图。

sources.title: Britannica: Jamestown Colony
Jamestown Rediscovery (Preservation Virginia): History of Jamestown
James Horn, A Land as God Made It: Jamestown and the Birth of America (2005)

story.en:
Three small ships, the Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery, carried 104 men and boys up the river they named for King James. They chose a marshy island for defence against Spain; its brackish water bred typhoid and dysentery. By the first winter fewer than forty were alive.

The English had settled in the land of Tsenacommacah, ruled by the paramount chief Wahunsenacawh, known as Powhatan, who at first saw them as possible allies and suppliers of metal tools. Captain John Smith traded and bullied for corn; his famous tale of being saved from execution by Powhatan's young daughter Pocahontas was published years later and may describe a ritual or be embroidered.

The winter of 1609–10, the "starving time", reduced about 300 colonists to some 60, and archaeologists have confirmed Smith's grim reports of cannibalism. The colony was saved by fresh ships and, from 1612, by John Rolfe's sweet tobacco. In 1619 Jamestown hosted the first elected assembly in English America.
story.zh:
“苏珊·康斯坦特”号、“神速”号和“发现”号三艘小船载着104名男子和少年，溯一条以詹姆斯国王命名的河流而上。为防备西班牙人，他们选中了一座沼泽岛，但那里的半咸水滋生伤寒和痢疾。到第一个冬天，活下来的人不足四十。

英国人定居的地方属于“策纳科马卡”，由大酋长瓦洪森纳考统治，他通称波瓦坦，起初视英国人为可能的盟友和金属工具的来源。约翰·史密斯上尉连哄带吓地换取玉米；他那个被波瓦坦的少女波卡洪塔斯从刑场救下的著名故事多年后才发表，描述的可能是一种仪式，也可能经过渲染。

1609至1610年冬天的“饥饿时期”使约300名殖民者锐减到60人左右，考古学家证实了史密斯关于人相食的骇人记载。新到的船只以及自1612年起约翰·罗尔夫培育的香甜烟草拯救了殖民地。1619年，詹姆斯敦召开了英属美洲第一个民选议会。

summary.en: On 3 July 1608 Samuel de Champlain began building a fortified trading post, the Habitation, at a narrowing of the St. Lawrence the Algonquin called kébec. Québec became the capital of New France and the cradle of French-speaking North America.
summary.zh: 1608年7月3日，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰在圣劳伦斯河收窄处开始修建设防的贸易据点“居所”，阿尔冈昆人称此地为“kébec”。魁北克后来成为新法兰西的首府，也是北美法语社会的摇篮。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Quebec City
Britannica: Samuel de Champlain
David Hackett Fischer, Champlain's Dream (2008)

story.en:
Champlain had already sailed the St. Lawrence in 1603 and spent hard winters in Acadia when he chose the cliff-backed shore below Cap Diamant, where the river narrows to about a kilometre. The Algonquian word kébec means "where the river narrows". His Habitation was a cluster of wooden buildings with a moat and a dovecote.

The first winter was brutal: of 28 men, scurvy and dysentery left eight alive by spring. Before that, Champlain had uncovered a plot by a locksmith, Jean Duval, to murder him and hand the post to Basque traders; Duval was hanged and his head displayed on a pike.

Québec's survival depended on alliances. In 1609 Champlain joined Wendat (Huron), Algonquin and Innu allies on a raid south into Mohawk country, where his arquebus killed two chiefs, a gesture that bound New France to its northern partners and set the Haudenosaunee against it for most of a century.
story.zh:
尚普兰在1603年就曾航行于圣劳伦斯河，也在阿卡迪亚熬过数个艰苦的冬天。他最终选中钻石岬下方背倚峭壁的河岸，那里河面收窄到约一公里宽。阿尔冈昆语“kébec”意为“河流变窄之处”。他的“居所”是一组带壕沟和鸽舍的木建筑。

第一个冬天极为严酷：28人中，坏血病和痢疾到春天只留下8人。此前，尚普兰还挫败了锁匠让·杜瓦尔谋杀他、把据点交给巴斯克商人的阴谋；杜瓦尔被绞死，首级挂在长矛上示众。

魁北克能否存续取决于结盟。1609年，尚普兰随温达特（休伦）、阿尔冈昆和因努盟友南下袭击莫霍克人的地盘，他用火绳枪击毙了两名酋长。这一举动把新法兰西与北方的伙伴绑在一起，也使豪德诺索尼人在近一个世纪里与之为敌。

summary.en: Governor Pedro de Peralta moved the capital of Spanish New Mexico to a new villa, La Villa Real de la Santa Fe, around 1610. Its adobe Palace of the Governors is the oldest continuously used public building in the United States.
summary.zh: 约1610年，总督佩德罗·德·佩拉尔塔将西属新墨西哥的首府迁至新建的“圣菲皇家镇”。镇上土坯建造的总督府是美国至今连续使用时间最长的公共建筑。

sources.title: Britannica: Santa Fe
New Mexico History Museum: Palace of the Governors
John L. Kessell, Spain in the Southwest (2002)

note: The villa was laid out in 1609–1610; 1610 is the conventional founding year.

name.en: First enslaved Africans in English Virginia
name.zh: 首批被奴役非洲人抵达英属弗吉尼亚

summary.en: In late August 1619 the privateer White Lion brought "20 and odd" Africans, captured from a Portuguese slave ship bound from Angola, to Point Comfort, Virginia, where they were traded for food. Their arrival is a symbolic starting point of African American history in the English colonies.
summary.zh: 1619年8月下旬，私掠船“白狮”号把从一艘自安哥拉驶出的葡萄牙奴隶船上劫来的“二十多名”非洲人带到弗吉尼亚的康福特角，用他们换取食物。这一事件被视为英属殖民地非裔美国人历史的象征性起点。

sources.title: National Park Service: Fort Monroe, 1619 – The Arrival of the First Africans
John Rolfe, letter to Sir Edwin Sandys (January 1620)
Encyclopedia Virginia: The First Africans

story.en:
The Africans were Kimbundu-speaking people from the kingdom of Ndongo in Angola, seized in Portuguese wars there and loaded aboard the slave ship São João Bautista for Veracruz. In the Gulf of Mexico two English privateers, the White Lion and the Treasurer, attacked it and took some of the captives.

The colonist John Rolfe recorded that a Dutch man-of-war (the White Lion, sailing under a Dutch commission) arrived at Point Comfort and sold the governor and the cape merchant "20 and odd Negroes" for provisions. Some of the captives were sent to plantations along the James River; one couple, Antony and Isabella, had a son baptised William, among the first children of African descent recorded in English America.

Their legal status at first was unclear, and a few early Africans in Virginia won freedom. But during the 17th century the colony wrote lifelong, inherited slavery into law, and by 1860 nearly four million people were enslaved in the United States.
story.zh:
这些非洲人是来自安哥拉恩东戈王国、说金本杜语的人，在葡萄牙人发动的战争中被俘，被装上开往韦拉克鲁斯的奴隶船“圣若昂·包蒂斯塔”号。在墨西哥湾，两艘英国私掠船“白狮”号和“司库”号袭击了这艘船，劫走了部分俘虏。

殖民者约翰·罗尔夫记载，一艘荷兰战舰（即持荷兰私掠许可的“白狮”号）抵达康福特角，把“二十多名黑人”卖给总督和殖民地商务官以换取补给。部分俘虏被送往詹姆斯河沿岸的种植园；其中一对名叫安东尼和伊莎贝拉的夫妇，生下一个受洗名为威廉的儿子，他是英属美洲最早有记录的非裔儿童之一。

他们最初的法律地位并不明确，弗吉尼亚早期也有少数非洲人获得自由。但在17世纪，殖民地逐步以法律确立了终身且世袭的奴隶制；到1860年，美国被奴役者已近四百万人。

name.zh: “五月花”号与普利茅斯殖民地

summary.en: English Separatists and other colonists crossed the Atlantic on the Mayflower, signed a compact of self-government off Cape Cod, and settled at Plymouth in December 1620 on the site of the Wampanoag village of Patuxet, emptied by an epidemic.
summary.zh: 英国分离派清教徒和其他殖民者乘“五月花”号横渡大西洋，在科德角外签署自治公约，并于1620年12月在万帕诺亚格人的村落帕图克塞特旧址定居普利茅斯，该村此前已因瘟疫人亡村空。

sources.title: Britannica: Plymouth
William Bradford, Of Plymouth Plantation (c. 1630–1651)
Plimoth Patuxet Museums

story.en:
The Mayflower left Plymouth, England, in September 1620 with 102 passengers, about a third of them religious Separatists who had first fled to Leiden in the Netherlands. Storms blew them far north of their Virginia patent. Because their charter did not apply to New England, 41 men signed a short agreement on 11 November (Old Style) to form a "civil body politic" and obey laws made in common, the Mayflower Compact.

They chose a cleared site with a good brook: Patuxet, whose Wampanoag inhabitants had died in an epidemic around 1617–19. Half the colonists died the first winter. In March 1621 an Abenaki man, Samoset, walked into the settlement and greeted them in English; he brought Tisquantum (Squanto), a Patuxet survivor who had been kidnapped to Spain and England, and the Wampanoag leader Massasoit, who made an alliance with them.

The harvest feast of autumn 1621, attended by Massasoit and about ninety of his men, later became the American Thanksgiving story.
story.zh:
1620年9月，“五月花”号载着102名乘客从英格兰普利茅斯起航，其中约三分之一是曾先避居荷兰莱顿的宗教分离派。风暴把他们吹到弗吉尼亚特许地以北很远的地方。由于特许状在新英格兰无效，41名男子于（旧历）11月11日签署了一份简短协议，组成“公民政治团体”并遵守共同制定的法律，即《五月花号公约》。

他们选中了一处已开垦、有好溪流的地方：帕图克塞特。那里的万帕诺亚格居民已在约1617至1619年的瘟疫中死去。殖民者在第一个冬天死了一半。1621年3月，一个名叫萨莫塞特的阿贝纳基人走进定居点，用英语向他们问好；他带来了帕图克塞特的幸存者提斯宽图（斯匡托）——此人曾被拐卖到西班牙和英格兰——以及与殖民者结盟的万帕诺亚格首领马萨索伊特。

1621年秋天，马萨索伊特带着约九十名手下参加了丰收宴会，这后来成为美国感恩节故事的由来。

name.en: New Amsterdam and the "purchase" of Manhattan
name.zh: 新阿姆斯特丹与曼哈顿“购买”

summary.en: Director Peter Minuit of the Dutch West India Company acquired Manhattan from Lenape people in 1626 for trade goods valued at 60 guilders, and Fort Amsterdam became the seat of New Netherland. The two sides likely understood the deal very differently.
summary.zh: 1626年，荷兰西印度公司总督彼得·米纽伊特以价值60荷兰盾的货物从莱纳佩人手中取得曼哈顿，阿姆斯特丹堡成为新尼德兰的治所。双方对这笔交易的理解很可能大相径庭。

sources.title: Pieter Schagen, letter to the States General, 5 November 1626 (Nationaal Archief, The Hague)
Britannica: New Netherland
Russell Shorto, The Island at the Center of the World (2004)

story.en:
The only contemporary evidence is a letter of November 1626 by Pieter Schagen, a Dutch official, reporting that the colonists had bought the island of Manhattes from the "wild men" for the value of 60 guilders. A 19th-century historian converted that into 24 dollars, giving birth to the legend of the cheapest real-estate deal in history.

For the Lenape, land was not property to be sold outright; an exchange of gifts likely granted the Dutch a right to share it. The Dutch built Fort Amsterdam at the island's southern tip, and the town of New Amsterdam grew around it: a polyglot trading port where, a visitor reported in the 1640s, eighteen languages were spoken.

The relationship soured. Director Willem Kieft's war on the Lenape (1643–45) killed hundreds. In 1664 an English fleet appeared, and Director Peter Stuyvesant surrendered without a shot; the town was renamed New York.
story.zh:
唯一的同时代证据是荷兰官员彼得·沙亨1626年11月的一封信，信中报告殖民者以价值60荷兰盾的货物从“野人”手里买下了曼哈托斯岛。一位19世纪的历史学家将其折算为24美元，于是诞生了“史上最便宜地产交易”的传说。

对莱纳佩人而言，土地并不是可以一卖了之的财产；交换礼物很可能只意味着允许荷兰人共同使用。荷兰人在岛南端修建了阿姆斯特丹堡，新阿姆斯特丹镇围绕它发展起来，成为一个多语种的贸易港口；据17世纪40年代的一位访客说，那里通行十八种语言。

双方关系逐渐恶化。总督威廉·基夫特对莱纳佩人发动的战争（1643—1645）造成数百人死亡。1664年一支英国舰队出现，总督彼得·斯泰弗森特未发一枪便投降，该镇随即更名为纽约。

name.zh: 维尔玛丽（蒙特利尔）建立

summary.en: Paul de Chomedey de Maisonneuve and Jeanne Mance led about fifty French colonists to found Ville-Marie on the island of Montréal on 17 May 1642, a Catholic mission settlement that grew into the fur-trade capital of New France.
summary.zh: 1642年5月17日，保罗·德·肖梅迪·德·迈松讷沃和让娜·曼斯率约五十名法国殖民者在蒙特利尔岛上建立维尔玛丽。这一天主教传教定居点后来发展为新法兰西的毛皮贸易中心。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Montréal
Pointe-à-Callière, Montréal Archaeology and History Complex
Britannica: Montreal

story.en:
Ville-Marie was the dream of a devout Paris society, the Société de Notre-Dame de Montréal, which wanted a mission town where Indigenous people would be converted. The governor at Québec thought the island, on the war road of the Haudenosaunee, was suicidal and urged them to settle closer; Maisonneuve answered that he would go even if every tree turned into an Iroquois.

The colonists landed at a small point where a stream met the St. Lawrence, close to where Jacques Cartier had visited the town of Hochelaga a century before. Jeanne Mance, a laywoman from Langres, founded the Hôtel-Dieu hospital, and Marguerite Bourgeoys, who arrived in 1653, opened the town's first school in 1658.

For two decades the settlement lived under siege, its men working the fields in armed groups. But its position at the meeting of the St. Lawrence and Ottawa rivers made it the natural gateway to the interior, and by 1700 Montréal was the base of the western fur trade.
story.zh:
维尔玛丽是巴黎一个虔诚团体“蒙特利尔圣母会”的梦想，他们希望建立一座使原住民皈依的传教城镇。魁北克总督认为这座位于豪德诺索尼人征战要道上的岛屿无异于送死，劝他们靠近魁北克定居；迈松讷沃回答说，即使每棵树都变成易洛魁人，他也要去。

殖民者在一条小溪汇入圣劳伦斯河的小岬角登陆，那里离一个世纪前雅克·卡蒂埃造访过的霍切拉加镇不远。来自朗格勒的平信徒女子让娜·曼斯创办了主宫医院；1653年来到这里的玛格丽特·布儒瓦于1658年开办了镇上第一所学校。

此后二十年，定居点一直处于围困之中，男人们要结成武装小队下地耕作。但它地处圣劳伦斯河与渥太华河交汇处，是通往内陆的天然门户；到1700年，蒙特利尔已成为西部毛皮贸易的基地。

name.en: Beaver Wars and the fall of Wendake
name.zh: 河狸战争与温达克的覆灭

summary.en: Competing for furs, captives and European trade, the Haudenosaunee fought a century of wars against the Wendat (Huron), their allies and New France. In 1649 Haudenosaunee war parties destroyed the Wendat homeland on Georgian Bay, scattering its people.
summary.zh: 为争夺毛皮、俘虏和欧洲贸易，豪德诺索尼人与温达特（休伦）人及其盟友、新法兰西打了一个世纪的仗。1649年，豪德诺索尼战团摧毁了乔治亚湾畔温达特人的家园，使其族人流离四散。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Iroquois Wars
Bruce G. Trigger, The Children of Aataentsic: A History of the Huron People to 1660 (1976)
Sainte-Marie among the Hurons (Ontario Heritage): History

note: The term "Beaver Wars" covers a long series of conflicts; scholars debate how far furs, as opposed to captive-taking "mourning wars", drove them.

story.en:
By the 1630s the Wendat confederacy, perhaps 20,000 people in fortified towns between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay, was the hub of New France's fur trade and home to the Jesuit mission of Sainte-Marie. Epidemics of smallpox and measles carried by traders and missionaries killed roughly half of them within a decade.

The Haudenosaunee, armed with muskets from Dutch traders at Fort Orange and also devastated by disease, waged "mourning wars" to replace their dead with captives. In March 1649 a force of about a thousand Mohawk and Seneca warriors stormed the mission towns of Taenhatentaron (Saint-Ignace) and Saint-Louis; the Jesuits Jean de Brébeuf and Gabriel Lalemant were tortured to death. The Jesuits burned Sainte-Marie themselves and fled with survivors to Christian Island, where many starved.

Wendat refugees went to Québec (their descendants live at Wendake today), to the west as the Wyandot, or were adopted into Haudenosaunee nations. The wars only ended with the Great Peace of Montréal in 1701.
story.zh:
到17世纪30年代，温达特联盟约有两万人，居住在锡姆科湖与乔治亚湾之间的设防城镇里，是新法兰西毛皮贸易的枢纽，也是耶稣会圣玛丽传教站所在地。商人和传教士带来的天花、麻疹疫情在十年内夺去了约一半人的生命。

豪德诺索尼人从奥兰治堡的荷兰商人那里获得火枪，自身也饱受疫病摧残，于是发动“哀悼战争”，以俘虏补充死者。1649年3月，约一千名莫霍克和塞内卡武士攻陷了传教镇泰恩哈滕塔隆（圣伊尼亚斯）和圣路易，耶稣会士让·德·布雷伯夫和加布里埃尔·拉勒芒被酷刑折磨致死。耶稣会士亲手焚毁圣玛丽，带着幸存者逃往基督徒岛，许多人在那里饿死。

温达特难民有的去了魁北克（其后裔至今生活在温达克），有的西迁成为怀安多特人，还有的被豪德诺索尼各族收养。直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》，这些战争才宣告结束。

summary.en: Puritan Massachusetts Bay and Connecticut, with Mohegan and Narragansett allies, crushed the Pequot of southern New England. At Mystic in May 1637 colonists burned a fortified village and killed some 400–700 people, many of them women and children.
summary.zh: 清教徒的马萨诸塞湾殖民地和康涅狄格殖民地联合莫希干人和纳拉甘西特人，击垮了新英格兰南部的佩克特人。1637年5月，殖民者在米斯蒂克焚毁一座设防村落，杀死约四百至七百人，其中许多是妇女和儿童。

sources.title: Britannica: Pequot War
Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center: The Pequot War
Alfred A. Cave, The Pequot War (1996)

name.zh: 哈德逊湾公司获颁特许状

summary.en: Charles II granted "the Governor and Company of Adventurers of England tradeing into Hudson's Bay" a monopoly over all lands draining into Hudson Bay, a territory later called Rupert's Land. Its posts such as York Factory dominated the northern fur trade for two centuries.
summary.zh: 查理二世授予“英格兰赴哈德逊湾贸易冒险者总督与公司”对所有流入哈德逊湾的河流流域的垄断权，这片土地后称鲁珀特地。约克工厂等商站在此后两个世纪里主导了北方的毛皮贸易。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Hudson's Bay Company
Britannica: Hudson's Bay Company
Archives of Manitoba: Hudson's Bay Company Archives

note: Pinned at York Factory, the company's main depot on the bay, rather than its London or Toronto head office.

story.en:
The company began with two French traders who could not get a hearing at home. Pierre-Esprit Radisson and his brother-in-law Médard Chouart des Groseilliers had learned from Cree partners that the best furs could be reached by sea through Hudson Bay, bypassing the long canoe routes of the St. Lawrence. Rebuffed and fined in New France, they went to London.

In 1668 the ketch Nonsuch, with Groseilliers aboard, wintered at James Bay and came home full of beaver pelts. Two years later Charles II chartered a company headed by his cousin Prince Rupert and gave it a vast territory most of its shareholders would never see.

The company's men mostly stayed at their bayside forts, and Cree and other First Nations traders brought furs down to them, often marrying into the posts' families. In 1870 the company sold Rupert's Land to the new Dominion of Canada; it survives today as one of the oldest companies in the world.
story.zh:
这家公司的起源是两个在本国得不到重视的法国商人。皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松和他的妹夫梅达尔·舒阿尔·德·格罗塞耶从克里族伙伴那里得知，最好的毛皮可以经哈德逊湾从海路获得，无需走圣劳伦斯河漫长的独木舟航道。他们在新法兰西碰了壁还被罚款，于是前往伦敦。

1668年，载着格罗塞耶的“无双”号双桅帆船在詹姆斯湾过冬，满载河狸皮返航。两年后，查理二世向一家由其表弟鲁珀特亲王领衔的公司颁发特许状，授予它一片大多数股东终生都不会见到的广袤土地。

公司职员大多留守在湾边的堡垒里，由克里族等原住民商人把毛皮运来，他们也常与商站家庭通婚。1870年，公司把鲁珀特地出售给新成立的加拿大自治领；它作为世界上最古老的公司之一延续至今。

summary.en: Metacom (called King Philip by the English), sachem of the Wampanoag, led a coalition of Native nations against the expanding New England colonies. Proportionally one of the deadliest wars in American history, it destroyed dozens of towns and ended with Metacom's death and the enslavement of many captives.
summary.zh: 万帕诺亚格酋长梅塔科姆（英国人称之为“菲利普国王”）领导多个原住民部族联合对抗不断扩张的新英格兰殖民地。按人口比例这是美国历史上最惨烈的战争之一，数十座城镇被毁，最终以梅塔科姆之死和大批俘虏被卖为奴告终。

sources.title: Britannica: King Philip's War
Jill Lepore, The Name of War: King Philip's War and the Origins of American Identity (1998)
Mary Rowlandson, The Sovereignty and Goodness of God (1682)

note: Fighting in southern New England ended in 1676; conflict in Maine continued until 1678.

story.en:
Fifty years after the Wampanoag leader Massasoit allied with the Plymouth settlers, his son Metacom watched colonists fence ever more land and summon his people before English courts. In 1675 Plymouth hanged three Wampanoag men for the murder of John Sassamon, a Christian Native informer, and fighting broke out at Swansea that June.

The war spread up the Connecticut River and into Maine as Nipmuc, Narragansett and other nations joined. Native forces attacked more than half of New England's ninety towns. Mary Rowlandson, taken captive at Lancaster, later wrote a bestselling account of her eleven weeks with her captors. In December 1675 colonial troops attacked the Narragansett in the Great Swamp Fight, killing hundreds.

Hunger, disease and Mohawk attacks wore down the coalition. In August 1676 Metacom was shot near Mount Hope; his head was displayed at Plymouth for some twenty years. His wife and son were among hundreds of captives sold into slavery in the West Indies.
story.zh:
万帕诺亚格首领马萨索伊特与普利茅斯移民结盟五十年后，他的儿子梅塔科姆眼看着殖民者圈占越来越多的土地，还把他的族人传唤到英国人的法庭上。1675年，普利茅斯以谋杀信奉基督教的原住民告密者约翰·萨萨蒙为由绞死了三名万帕诺亚格男子，同年6月斯旺西爆发战斗。

随着尼普穆克、纳拉甘西特等部族加入，战火蔓延到康涅狄格河流域和缅因。原住民武装袭击了新英格兰九十座城镇中的一半以上。在兰开斯特被俘的玛丽·罗兰森后来写下她十一周俘虏生活的记述，成为畅销书。1675年12月，殖民地军队在“大沼泽之战”中袭击纳拉甘西特人，杀死数百人。

饥饿、疾病和莫霍克人的袭击使原住民联盟日渐不支。1676年8月，梅塔科姆在希望山附近被击毙，他的首级在普利茅斯示众约二十年。他的妻儿与数百名俘虏一起被卖到西印度群岛为奴。

summary.en: In a coordinated uprising organised by Po'pay of Ohkay Owingeh, the Pueblo peoples of New Mexico killed some 400 Spaniards, including 21 Franciscan friars, besieged Santa Fe and drove the colonists south to El Paso. The Pueblos stayed independent for twelve years.
summary.zh: 在奥凯奥文格的波佩组织下，新墨西哥的普韦布洛诸民族协同起事，杀死约400名西班牙人（包括21名方济各会修士），围困圣菲，把殖民者赶到南方的埃尔帕索。普韦布洛人此后保持了十二年的独立。

sources.title: Britannica: Pueblo Rebellion
Andrew L. Knaut, The Pueblo Revolt of 1680 (1995)
Joe S. Sando & Herman Agoyo (eds.), Po'pay: Leader of the First American Revolution (2005)

story.en:
Eight decades of Spanish rule in New Mexico had brought forced labour, tribute in corn and blankets, and a campaign by Franciscan missionaries to stamp out kachina dances and kivas. In 1675 Governor Juan Francisco Treviño had 47 Pueblo religious leaders arrested for sorcery; three were hanged, one took his own life and the rest were whipped. One of those released was a Tewa man named Po'pay.

From Taos Pueblo, Po'pay and other leaders planned a revolt across dozens of towns speaking different languages. Runners carried knotted cords, one knot to be untied each day until the rising. When two messengers were captured, the date was moved forward to 10 August 1680. Priests and settlers were killed across the province, and some 2,500 Pueblo warriors besieged Santa Fe until Governor Antonio de Otermín broke out and led the survivors to El Paso.

Churches were burned and Christian marriages dissolved. Diego de Vargas reoccupied Santa Fe in 1692, but the Spanish who returned largely tolerated Pueblo religion, and the land grants they recognised underpin Pueblo lands today.
story.zh:
西班牙统治新墨西哥的八十年间，带来了强迫劳役、以玉米和毛毯缴纳的贡赋，以及方济各会传教士禁绝卡奇纳舞蹈和基瓦的运动。1675年，总督胡安·弗朗西斯科·特雷维尼奥以巫术罪逮捕了47名普韦布洛宗教领袖，三人被绞死，一人自尽，其余遭鞭打。获释者中有一位名叫波佩的特瓦人。

波佩与其他首领以陶斯普韦布洛为据点，策划在数十个语言各异的村镇同时起事。信使们传递打了结的绳子，每天解开一个结，直到起义之日。两名信使被捕后，起义提前到1680年8月10日。全省各地的神父和移民遭到杀戮，约2500名普韦布洛武士围困圣菲，直到总督安东尼奥·德·奥特明突围，率幸存者退往埃尔帕索。

教堂被焚毁，基督教婚姻被宣布解除。1692年迭戈·德·巴尔加斯重新占领圣菲，但返回的西班牙人大体容忍了普韦布洛宗教，他们当时承认的土地授予至今仍是普韦布洛土地权的基础。

summary.en: After girls in Salem Village, Massachusetts, began suffering fits in early 1692, more than 150 people were accused of witchcraft. A special court hanged nineteen and one man was pressed to death before the governor halted the trials and colonists, including several judges, later repented.
summary.zh: 1692年初马萨诸塞塞勒姆村的几个女孩开始出现抽搐症状，此后150多人被控施行巫术。特别法庭处绞19人，另有一名男子被重石压死，直到总督叫停审判；后来包括几位法官在内的殖民者公开忏悔。

sources.title: Britannica: Salem witch trials
Mary Beth Norton, In the Devil's Snare: The Salem Witchcraft Crisis of 1692 (2002)
University of Virginia: Salem Witch Trials Documentary Archive

story.en:
In January 1692 Betty Parris, the nine-year-old daughter of Salem Village's minister, and her cousin Abigail Williams began to scream, contort and complain of being pinched by invisible hands. Pressed to name their tormentors, they accused Tituba, an enslaved woman of the household, and two poor local women. Tituba confessed to seeing the Devil, giving the panic its script.

Accusations spread to dozens of villages. The Court of Oyer and Terminer accepted "spectral evidence", testimony that the accused's spirit had appeared to the victim, which no defendant could disprove. Those who confessed were spared; those who maintained innocence, such as the elderly church member Rebecca Nurse, were hanged on Gallows Hill. Giles Corey, who refused to plead, was crushed under stones.

Historians link the crisis to frontier war with the Wabanaki, which had filled Essex County with refugees and fear. In October Governor William Phips stopped the trials, reportedly after his own wife was named. In 1697 judge Samuel Sewall publicly asked forgiveness.
story.zh:
1692年1月，塞勒姆村牧师九岁的女儿贝蒂·帕里斯和她的表姐阿比盖尔·威廉斯开始尖叫、身体扭曲，并抱怨被看不见的手掐拧。在逼问下，她们指控了家中女奴蒂图巴和两名贫穷的本地妇女。蒂图巴供认见过魔鬼，为这场恐慌提供了“剧本”。

指控蔓延到数十个村镇。审理法庭采纳了“幽灵证据”，即证人声称被告的灵魂曾出现在受害者面前，被告根本无法反驳。认罪者得以免死，坚称无辜者——如年迈的教会成员丽贝卡·纳斯——则在绞刑山上被处死。拒绝答辩的贾尔斯·科里被石块压死。

史学家把这场危机与对瓦巴纳基人的边境战争联系起来，战争使埃塞克斯县充满难民和恐惧。10月，总督威廉·菲普斯叫停审判，据说是在他自己的妻子也遭指控之后。1697年，法官塞缪尔·休厄尔公开请求宽恕。

summary.en: On the night of 26 January 1700 the Cascadia subduction zone ruptured along some 1,000 km from Vancouver Island to northern California, in a magnitude ~9 earthquake. Its tsunami crossed the Pacific and was recorded in Japan, allowing scientists to date it to the hour.
summary.zh: 1700年1月26日夜，卡斯凯迪亚俯冲带从温哥华岛到北加利福尼亚约1000公里的断层破裂，发生约9级大地震。地震引发的海啸横越太平洋，在日本留下记录，使科学家得以把它精确定时到小时。

sources.title: Brian F. Atwater et al., The Orphan Tsunami of 1700 (USGS Professional Paper 1707, 2005)
Satake et al., "Time and size of a giant earthquake in Cascadia inferred from Japanese tsunami records of January 1700", Nature 379 (1996)
Britannica: Cascadia subduction zone

story.en:
For centuries the Pacific Northwest seemed free of great earthquakes, though Indigenous peoples of the coast, from the Nuu-chah-nulth to the Yurok, told stories of shaking ground and floods that swept away villages, sometimes as a battle between Thunderbird and Whale.

In the 1980s geologists found "ghost forests" of dead red cedars standing in tidal marshes in Washington and Oregon, killed when the coast suddenly dropped and salt water flooded their roots. Tree rings showed they had died between the growing seasons of 1699 and 1700.

The final clue came from Japan. Merchants and officials along the coast of Honshu had recorded a tsunami of up to several metres that arrived around midnight on a day in the year Genroku 12 with no earthquake felt. Working backwards across the Pacific, seismologists placed the Cascadia rupture at about 9 p.m. local time on 26 January 1700. The discovery transformed building codes and tsunami planning in the region.
story.zh:
几个世纪以来，太平洋西北地区似乎从无大地震，但从努恰努尔斯人到尤罗克人，沿海原住民都流传着大地摇晃、洪水冲走村庄的故事，有时被讲述为雷鸟与鲸的搏斗。

20世纪80年代，地质学家在华盛顿州和俄勒冈州的潮汐沼泽中发现了成片枯死却仍然直立的红雪松“幽灵森林”：海岸骤然下沉，咸水淹没树根，使它们死去。树轮显示，这些树死于1699年与1700年两个生长季之间。

最后的线索来自日本。本州沿岸的商人和官员记载，元禄十二年某日午夜前后，在没有感到地震的情况下，有一场高达数米的海啸袭来。地震学家横跨太平洋逆推，确定卡斯凯迪亚破裂发生在1700年1月26日当地时间晚上9点左右。这一发现彻底改变了该地区的建筑规范和海啸防范。

summary.en: Governor Louis-Hector de Callière and representatives of some 39 Indigenous nations, including the Haudenosaunee and the Great Lakes allies of New France, ratified a general peace at Montréal, ending nearly a century of the Beaver Wars.
summary.zh: 总督路易-埃克托尔·德·卡利埃尔与约39个原住民民族的代表——包括豪德诺索尼人和新法兰西在五大湖地区的盟友——在蒙特利尔批准了一项全面和约，结束了近一个世纪的河狸战争。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Great Peace of Montreal (1701)
Gilles Havard, The Great Peace of Montreal of 1701: French-Native Diplomacy in the Seventeenth Century (2001)
Pointe-à-Callière: The Great Peace of Montréal

story.en:
In the summer of 1701 some 1,300 delegates paddled to Montréal from as far as the Mississippi and Lake Superior, the largest diplomatic gathering the colony had ever seen. An epidemic was raging and many fell ill on the way.

The negotiations hinged on the Wendat chief Kondiaronk, known to the French as "the Rat", a brilliant orator who had once wrecked a peace by deception and now worked to secure one. He fell sick and died during the talks after a long speech to the assembly; the French gave him a grand funeral, and he was buried in Montréal's church.

On 4 August each nation's delegates signed the treaty with a pictograph of its clan animal. The nations agreed to bring disputes to the governor rather than take revenge, and the Haudenosaunee promised neutrality in wars between France and England. The peace held in the Great Lakes for decades and is still commemorated by Indigenous nations and in Québec.
story.zh:
1701年夏，约1300名代表从远至密西西比河和苏必利尔湖的地方划着独木舟来到蒙特利尔，这是殖民地有史以来规模最大的外交聚会。当时正值瘟疫流行，许多人在途中病倒。

谈判的关键人物是温达特酋长孔迪亚龙克，法国人称他为“老鼠”。这位出色的演说家曾用诡计破坏过一次和谈，此时却全力促成和平。他在向大会发表长篇演说后病倒，于谈判期间去世；法国人为他举行了隆重的葬礼，将他安葬在蒙特利尔的教堂里。

8月4日，各民族代表以本氏族的动物图形在和约上签字。各族同意把争端交由总督裁决而不再自行复仇，豪德诺索尼人承诺在英法战争中保持中立。这一和平在五大湖地区维持了数十年，至今仍为原住民各族和魁北克所纪念。

summary.en: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville founded La Nouvelle-Orléans on a crescent of high ground beside the Mississippi in 1718, naming it for the regent Philippe d'Orléans. It became the capital of French Louisiana in 1722 and passed to Spain in 1763.
summary.zh: 1718年，让-巴蒂斯特·勒莫瓦纳·德·比安维尔在密西西比河畔一片新月形高地上建立新奥尔良，以摄政王奥尔良公爵腓力命名。1722年它成为法属路易斯安那首府，1763年转归西班牙。

sources.title: Britannica: New Orleans
Lawrence N. Powell, The Accidental City: Improvising New Orleans (2012)
The Historic New Orleans Collection: 64 Parishes

summary.en: A wave of emotional Protestant revivals swept the British colonies, led by preachers such as Jonathan Edwards in Northampton and the English itinerant George Whitefield, who drew crowds of thousands. The revivals split churches, spread evangelical religion among enslaved Africans and loosened the hold of established clergy.
summary.zh: 一股情感炽烈的新教复兴浪潮席卷英属各殖民地，代表人物有北安普敦的乔纳森·爱德华兹和英国巡回布道家乔治·怀特菲尔德，后者的布道动辄吸引数千听众。复兴运动造成教会分裂，使福音派信仰在被奴役的非洲人中传播，也削弱了建制派神职人员的影响。

sources.title: Britannica: Great Awakening
Thomas S. Kidd, The Great Awakening: The Roots of Evangelical Christianity in Colonial America (2007)

note: Dates for the revival vary; 1734 marks the Northampton revival, and the peak followed Whitefield's 1739–1741 tour.

name.zh: 白令与奇里科夫抵达阿拉斯加

summary.en: On Russia's Great Northern Expedition, the ships of Vitus Bering and Aleksei Chirikov crossed from Kamchatka and sighted the Alaskan coast in July 1741. The naturalist Georg Steller spent ten hours on Kayak Island; on the return Bering died after being wrecked on the island now named for him.
summary.zh: 在俄国大北方考察中，维图斯·白令和阿列克谢·奇里科夫的船只从堪察加出发，于1741年7月望见阿拉斯加海岸。博物学家格奥尔格·斯特勒在卡亚克岛上停留了十个小时；返航途中白令在以他命名的岛上遇难身亡。

sources.title: Britannica: Vitus Bering
Georg Wilhelm Steller, Journal of a Voyage with Bering, 1741–1742 (ed. O. W. Frost, 1988)
Orcutt Frost, Bering: The Russian Discovery of America (2003)

note: The QID is for the whole Great Northern Expedition (1733–1743); this record marks its American voyage.

story.en:
Peter the Great had asked whether Asia and America were joined. Vitus Bering, a Danish officer in Russian service, partly answered the question in 1728, but fog hid the American shore. His second, far larger expedition took a decade of hauling men and supplies across Siberia before two ships, the St. Peter and St. Paul, sailed from Kamchatka in June 1741.

The ships lost each other in a storm. Chirikov reached the Alexander Archipelago, where two boats sent ashore never returned. Bering sighted Mount St. Elias on 16 July and anchored at Kayak Island, but, anxious about the season, he allowed the German naturalist Georg Steller only ten hours ashore. Steller still collected a jay later named for him and dozens of plants new to science, and complained bitterly that ten years of preparation had bought ten hours of study.

On the way home scurvy ravaged the crew and the St. Peter was wrecked on an uninhabited island. Bering died there in December. The survivors built a boat from the wreck and returned with sea otter pelts, starting the Russian fur rush into Alaska.
story.zh:
彼得大帝曾想知道亚洲和美洲是否相连。为俄国效力的丹麦军官维图斯·白令在1728年部分回答了这个问题，但大雾遮住了美洲海岸。他的第二次远征规模大得多，花了十年时间把人员和物资运过西伯利亚，直到1741年6月，“圣彼得”号和“圣保罗”号才从堪察加起航。

两船在风暴中失散。奇里科夫抵达亚历山大群岛，派上岸的两艘小艇一去不返。白令于7月16日望见圣埃利亚斯山，并在卡亚克岛下锚，但他担心季节已晚，只允许德国博物学家格奥尔格·斯特勒上岸十个小时。斯特勒仍采集到一种后来以他命名的松鸦和数十种新植物，并愤懑地抱怨十年准备只换来十小时考察。

返航途中坏血病肆虐，“圣彼得”号在一座无人岛上触礁失事，白令于12月死在那里。幸存者用残骸造了一条船，带着海獭皮返回，由此掀起俄国人涌入阿拉斯加的毛皮热潮。

summary.en: The North American theatre of the Seven Years' War pitted Britain and its colonies against New France and its Indigenous allies. After early French victories, British sea power and money took Louisbourg, Québec and Montréal, and in 1763 France ceded Canada and the land east of the Mississippi.
summary.zh: 作为七年战争的北美战场，这场战争是英国及其殖民地与新法兰西及其原住民盟友之间的较量。法国在初期屡获胜利，但英国凭借海上优势和财力攻占了路易斯堡、魁北克和蒙特利尔；1763年法国割让加拿大和密西西比河以东的土地。

label.zh: 必需堡：华盛顿投降
布拉多克在莫农加希拉河畔战败
威廉·亨利堡陷落
法军在卡里永（提康德罗加）获胜
英军攻占路易斯堡
法军放弃迪凯纳堡
魁北克亚伯拉罕平原
蒙特利尔投降

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Seven Years' War
Britannica: French and Indian War
Fred Anderson, Crucible of War: The Seven Years' War and the Fate of Empire in British North America, 1754–1766 (2000)

story.en:
The war began in the Ohio valley, which both empires claimed. In May 1754 a 22-year-old Virginia militia officer, George Washington, ambushed a French party at Jumonville Glen; its commander was killed, possibly by Washington's Seneca ally Tanacharison. Weeks later Washington surrendered his hastily built Fort Necessity. Horace Walpole later wrote that a volley fired by a young Virginian in the backwoods set the world on fire.

For three years New France and its Indigenous allies won: General Braddock's army was destroyed near Fort Duquesne in 1755, and the Marquis de Montcalm took Oswego and Fort William Henry. Then William Pitt poured British money, regulars and ships into America. Louisbourg fell in 1758, Québec in 1759, Montréal in 1760.

By the Treaty of Paris (1763) France gave up New France; Spain took Louisiana west of the Mississippi. But the victory left Britain deeply in debt and its colonists no longer in need of protection against France, a combination that would lead to revolution.
story.zh:
战争始于两大帝国都声称拥有的俄亥俄河谷。1754年5月，22岁的弗吉尼亚民兵军官乔治·华盛顿在朱蒙维尔峡谷伏击了一支法军小队，其指挥官被杀，凶手可能是华盛顿的塞内卡盟友塔纳查里森。几周后，华盛顿在仓促修建的必需堡投降。霍勒斯·沃波尔后来写道，一个年轻的弗吉尼亚人在荒野里打出的一轮枪声点燃了整个世界。

头三年，新法兰西及其原住民盟友节节胜利：1755年布拉多克将军的部队在迪凯纳堡附近全军覆没，蒙卡尔姆侯爵又攻下奥斯威戈和威廉·亨利堡。随后威廉·皮特向美洲投入大量英国资金、正规军和战舰。路易斯堡于1758年、魁北克于1759年、蒙特利尔于1760年相继陷落。

根据1763年《巴黎条约》，法国放弃新法兰西，西班牙得到密西西比河以西的路易斯安那。但胜利使英国债台高筑，而殖民者也不再需要英国保护他们免受法国威胁，这两者结合最终导向了革命。

name.en: Expulsion of the Acadians (Le Grand Dérangement)
name.zh: 驱逐阿卡迪亚人（大动荡）

summary.en: British authorities in Nova Scotia deported some 10,000–11,500 French-speaking Acadians who refused an unconditional oath of allegiance, burning their farms and scattering them across the Thirteen Colonies, Britain and France. Thousands died; many later resettled in Louisiana as Cajuns.
summary.zh: 新斯科舍的英国当局把约一万至一万一千五百名拒绝无条件效忠宣誓的法语阿卡迪亚人驱逐出境，焚烧他们的农庄，把他们分散流放到十三殖民地、英国和法国。数千人死去；许多人后来在路易斯安那定居，成为“卡津人”。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Acadian Expulsion (the Great Upheaval)
John Mack Faragher, A Great and Noble Scheme: The Tragic Story of the Expulsion of the French Acadians (2005)
UNESCO World Heritage: Landscape of Grand Pré

story.en:
The Acadians had farmed the marshes around the Bay of Fundy since the 1630s, building dykes with sluice gates (aboiteaux) to turn tidal flats into fields. Britain gained Acadia in 1713, but for four decades the Acadians insisted on neutrality, refusing to swear an oath that might force them to fight France.

In 1755, with war resuming, Lieutenant Governor Charles Lawrence and his council decided to remove them. At Grand-Pré on 5 September, Lieutenant Colonel John Winslow summoned the men to the church and read the order that their lands and livestock were forfeit and they were to be deported. Families were loaded onto ships, sometimes separated, and the villages burned behind them.

Over the next eight years about three-quarters of the Acadians were expelled; shipwreck and smallpox killed many. Some escaped into the woods or to Québec. After 1764 many found their way to Spanish Louisiana. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's poem Evangeline (1847) made their exile famous, and in 2003 a royal proclamation acknowledged the wrongs done to them.
story.zh:
自17世纪30年代起，阿卡迪亚人就在芬迪湾周围的沼泽地耕作，他们修筑带闸门的堤坝（aboiteaux），把潮滩变成良田。1713年英国取得阿卡迪亚，但四十年来阿卡迪亚人坚持中立，拒绝宣誓效忠，以免被迫与法国作战。

1755年战事再起，副总督查尔斯·劳伦斯及其参事会决定把他们迁走。9月5日，约翰·温斯洛中校在大普雷把男人们召集到教堂，宣读命令：他们的土地和牲畜一律没收，本人将被驱逐。一家家人被装上船，有时被拆散，身后的村庄被付之一炬。

此后八年间，约四分之三的阿卡迪亚人被驱逐，许多人死于海难和天花。也有人逃入森林或投奔魁北克。1764年后，许多人辗转来到西属路易斯安那。亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗的长诗《伊万杰琳》（1847）使他们的流亡广为人知；2003年，一份王室公告承认了他们所遭受的不公。

name.en: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

summary.en: British troops under James Wolfe climbed the cliffs above the St. Lawrence at night and defeated the Marquis de Montcalm's army outside Québec in a battle of about fifteen minutes. Both generals were mortally wounded, and Québec surrendered five days later.
summary.zh: 詹姆斯·沃尔夫率英军夜间攀上圣劳伦斯河畔的悬崖，在魁北克城外与蒙卡尔姆侯爵的军队交战，约十五分钟便击败法军。两位统帅均受致命伤，魁北克五天后投降。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
Britannica: Battle of Quebec
D. Peter MacLeod, Northern Armageddon: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham (2008)

story.en:
All summer of 1759 Wolfe's army and fleet sat below Québec, bombarding the town to rubble but unable to draw Montcalm out of his entrenchments. Sick and running out of time before the river froze, Wolfe gambled. On the night of 12–13 September boats drifted downstream to a cove, the Anse au Foulon; a French-speaking officer is said to have answered a sentry's challenge, and light infantry scrambled up a steep path to overpower the guard post.

By morning some 4,500 redcoats stood on the Plains of Abraham, farmland west of the walls. Montcalm attacked at once rather than wait for reinforcements. His mixed line of regulars and militia advanced unevenly; the British held their fire until close range and broke it with volleys.

Wolfe was shot several times and died on the field; Montcalm, hit while retreating, died the next morning. Québec surrendered on 18 September. A French counter-attack at Sainte-Foy in April 1760 won the field but not the town, and when British ships arrived first in the spring, New France was lost.
story.zh:
1759年整个夏天，沃尔夫的陆军和舰队停在魁北克下方，把城镇炸成废墟，却无法把蒙卡尔姆诱出工事。沃尔夫身患疾病，又必须赶在河流封冻前结束战事，于是孤注一掷。9月12日至13日夜，小船顺流漂到富隆湾；据说一名会说法语的军官应付了哨兵的盘问，轻步兵沿陡峭小径攀上崖顶，制服了哨所。

到早晨，约4500名英国红衫军已列阵于城墙以西的农田亚伯拉罕平原。蒙卡尔姆没有等待援军，立即发起进攻。他由正规军和民兵混编的战线推进得参差不齐；英军一直等到近距离才开火，以齐射击溃了法军。

沃尔夫身中数弹，死于战场；蒙卡尔姆在撤退时中弹，次日清晨去世。魁北克于9月18日投降。1760年4月，法军在圣富瓦反攻，赢得了战场却没能夺回城市；春天英国船只抢先抵达，新法兰西就此失落。

summary.en: Angered by British policies after the defeat of France, a confederation of Great Lakes and Ohio valley nations inspired by the Odawa leader Pontiac and the Delaware prophet Neolin seized eight British forts in 1763 and besieged Detroit and Fort Pitt.
summary.zh: 法国战败后，五大湖与俄亥俄河谷诸民族对英国政策极为不满，在渥太华族首领庞蒂亚克和特拉华先知尼奥林的感召下结成联盟，于1763年夺取八座英国堡垒，并围攻底特律和皮特堡。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Pontiac's War
Gregory Evans Dowd, War under Heaven: Pontiac, the Indian Nations, and the British Empire (2002)
Britannica: Pontiac's War

story.en:
When the French surrendered, the British commander Jeffery Amherst cut off the gifts of powder, cloth and tools that French officers had given as signs of alliance, and treated the western nations as conquered peoples. A Delaware prophet, Neolin, preached that Native people must reject European goods and drive out the British.

In May 1763 Pontiac attempted to seize Detroit by surprise and, when that failed, laid siege to it. Within weeks warriors of many nations captured forts from Michilimackinac, where Ojibwe players chased a lacrosse ball through the gate, to Presque Isle on Lake Erie. At besieged Fort Pitt, officers gave Delaware envoys blankets from the smallpox hospital in hope of spreading disease, an episode documented in the fort's records.

Neither side could win outright. The war pushed London to issue the Proclamation of 1763, reserving the western lands for Indigenous peoples, and to restore gift-giving diplomacy. Pontiac made peace in 1766 and was killed in 1769 in Illinois.
story.zh:
法国投降后，英军总司令杰弗里·阿默斯特停止了法国军官以往作为结盟象征赠送的火药、布匹和工具，并把西部诸民族当作被征服者对待。特拉华先知尼奥林宣扬原住民必须拒绝欧洲货物，把英国人赶走。

1763年5月，庞蒂亚克企图突袭夺取底特律，未果后便围城。几周之内，许多民族的武士攻下了从米奇利马基纳克到伊利湖畔普雷斯克岛的一系列堡垒；在米奇利马基纳克，奥吉布瓦人借追逐一只长曲棍球冲进了堡门。在被围的皮特堡，军官们把天花病房的毯子送给特拉华使者，企图传播疾病，此事见于该堡的记录。

双方都无法取得完胜。战争促使伦敦颁布《1763年公告》，把西部土地保留给原住民，并恢复了赠礼外交。庞蒂亚克于1766年议和，1769年在伊利诺伊被杀。

summary.en: George III's proclamation organised the territories won from France and drew a line along the Appalachians beyond which colonists could not settle; Indigenous land could be acquired only by the Crown through public treaty. Resented in the colonies, it remains a foundation of Indigenous rights in Canada.
summary.zh: 乔治三世颁布的公告对从法国夺得的领土作出安排，并沿阿巴拉契亚山脉划定界线，禁止殖民者越线定居；原住民土地只能由王室通过公开条约取得。它在殖民地遭到怨恨，至今仍是加拿大原住民权利的基石之一。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Royal Proclamation of 1763
Britannica: Proclamation of 1763
Colin G. Calloway, The Scratch of a Pen: 1763 and the Transformation of North America (2006)

note: Pinned on the Appalachian crest along the proclamation line; the document was issued in London.

summary.en: Protesting the Tea Act and taxation without representation, colonists disguised as Mohawks boarded three ships at Griffin's Wharf and dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor. Parliament answered with the Coercive Acts, pushing the colonies toward rebellion.
summary.zh: 为抗议《茶税法》和“无代表不纳税”，殖民者装扮成莫霍克人登上格里芬码头的三艘船，把东印度公司的342箱茶叶倒入波士顿港。议会以《强制法令》回击，把殖民地推向反叛。

sources.title: Britannica: Boston Tea Party
Benjamin L. Carp, Defiance of the Patriots: The Boston Tea Party and the Making of America (2010)
Massachusetts Historical Society: The Boston Tea Party

story.en:
The Tea Act of 1773 actually made tea cheaper. It let the struggling East India Company ship directly to chosen colonial agents, undercutting smugglers, while keeping a small duty that Parliament insisted it had the right to levy. To many colonists, buying it meant accepting that right.

In Philadelphia and New York the tea ships were turned back. In Boston Governor Thomas Hutchinson, two of whose sons were tea agents, refused to let the ships leave without unloading. On the evening of 16 December, after a mass meeting at the Old South Meeting House broke up, a hundred or more men, some smeared with soot and wrapped in blankets as "Mohawks", spent three hours splitting chests on the Dartmouth, Eleanor and Beaver and tipping the tea overboard. Little else was damaged; a broken padlock was reportedly replaced.

London was outraged. The Coercive Acts of 1774 closed the port of Boston and curbed Massachusetts self-government, and the other colonies rallied to Boston in the First Continental Congress.
story.zh:
1773年的《茶税法》其实让茶叶更便宜了。它允许陷入困境的东印度公司直接把茶叶运给选定的殖民地代理商，从而压低走私茶的价格，同时保留一小笔关税，议会坚称自己有权征收。在许多殖民者看来，买这种茶就等于承认这一权力。

在费城和纽约，运茶船被拒之门外。在波士顿，总督托马斯·哈钦森（他的两个儿子就是茶叶代理商）不准船只不卸货就离港。12月16日傍晚，老南会堂的群众大会散会后，一百多名男子——有的脸上抹着煤灰、身裹毯子扮作“莫霍克人”——在“达特茅斯”号、“埃莉诺”号和“海狸”号上花了三个小时劈开茶箱，把茶叶倒进海里。其他东西几乎未受损坏，据说连一把被弄坏的挂锁也换了新的。

伦敦震怒。1774年的《强制法令》封闭了波士顿港，削减了马萨诸塞的自治权，其他殖民地则在第一届大陆会议上声援波士顿。

name.zh: 列克星敦和康科德战役

summary.en: British regulars marching to seize militia arms at Concord exchanged fire with minutemen on Lexington Green at dawn, then fought their way back to Boston under constant attack. The skirmishes opened the American Revolutionary War.
summary.zh: 英国正规军前往康科德收缴民兵武器，黎明时分在列克星敦草坪与“一分钟人”民兵交火，随后在不断的袭击中一路苦战退回波士顿。这几场小规模战斗揭开了美国独立战争的序幕。

sources.title: Britannica: Battles of Lexington and Concord
David Hackett Fischer, Paul Revere's Ride (1994)
National Park Service: Minute Man National Historical Park

summary.en: Thirteen British colonies fought for and won independence. The Continental Army under George Washington survived early defeats; victory at Saratoga brought France into the war, and the surrender of Cornwallis at Yorktown in 1781 led to the Treaty of Paris (1783), in which Britain recognised the United States.
summary.zh: 英国在北美的十三个殖民地为独立而战并取得胜利。乔治·华盛顿领导的大陆军挺过了初期的失败；萨拉托加大捷使法国参战，1781年康沃利斯在约克镇投降，最终促成1783年《巴黎条约》，英国承认美国独立。

波士顿邦克山
美军进攻魁北克失败

sources.title: Britannica: American Revolution
Gordon S. Wood, The American Revolution: A History (2002)
Robert Middlekauff, The Glorious Cause: The American Revolution, 1763–1789 (rev. ed., 2005)

story.en:
When fighting began in 1775, the colonies had no army, no navy and no government beyond a Continental Congress of delegates. Congress made George Washington, a Virginia planter and veteran of the French and Indian War, commander of the militias besieging Boston. He forced the British out in March 1776, then lost New York and retreated across New Jersey. On the night after Christmas he recrossed the ice-choked Delaware and captured a Hessian garrison at Trenton, a small victory that saved the cause.

The turning point came in October 1777, when General John Burgoyne's army, marching south from Canada, surrendered at Saratoga. France, already secretly supplying the Americans, signed an alliance in 1778; Spain and the Netherlands followed. The war became global.

Britain shifted to the South and took Savannah and Charleston, but a bitter partisan war wore its armies down. In 1781 a French fleet closed Chesapeake Bay while Washington and the Comte de Rochambeau trapped Lord Cornwallis at Yorktown. The war divided Indigenous nations too, and many, like the Mohawk leader Joseph Brant, fought for the Crown and lost their lands in the peace.
story.zh:
1775年战事爆发时，殖民地既无陆军也无海军，除了由各地代表组成的大陆会议外也没有政府。大陆会议任命弗吉尼亚种植园主、法国—印第安人战争老兵乔治·华盛顿统率围攻波士顿的民兵。1776年3月他迫使英军撤出波士顿，随后失去纽约，一路退过新泽西。圣诞节次日夜，他再次横渡冰凌堵塞的特拉华河，在特伦顿俘获一支黑森雇佣军守备队，这场小胜挽救了革命事业。

转折点出现在1777年10月：约翰·伯戈因将军从加拿大南下的军队在萨拉托加投降。早已秘密援助美国的法国于1778年与之结盟，西班牙和荷兰随后参战，战争演变为全球冲突。

英国转向南方，攻下萨凡纳和查尔斯顿，但残酷的游击战拖垮了它的军队。1781年，法国舰队封锁切萨皮克湾，华盛顿与罗尚博伯爵把康沃利斯勋爵围困在约克镇。战争也使原住民各民族分裂，许多人——如莫霍克首领约瑟夫·布兰特——站在英王一边作战，并在和约中失去了自己的土地。

summary.en: Meeting in the Pennsylvania State House in Philadelphia, the Second Continental Congress voted for independence on 2 July 1776 and adopted on 4 July a declaration drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson, proclaiming that all men are created equal with unalienable rights.
summary.zh: 第二届大陆会议在费城宾夕法尼亚州议会大厦开会，于1776年7月2日表决通过独立，7月4日通过了主要由托马斯·杰斐逊起草的宣言，宣告人人生而平等，享有不可剥夺的权利。

sources.title: National Archives (US): Declaration of Independence: A Transcription
Britannica: Declaration of Independence
Pauline Maier, American Scripture: Making the Declaration of Independence (1997)

story.en:
In June 1776 Congress appointed five men to draft a declaration; they handed the task to the 33-year-old Thomas Jefferson, who wrote it in rented rooms on Market Street in about two weeks. John Adams and Benjamin Franklin made small changes. Its opening passage set out a theory of government by consent, but most of the text was a list of grievances against George III.

Congress voted for independence on 2 July (Adams predicted that day would be celebrated for ever) and then spent two days editing Jefferson's draft, cutting about a quarter of it. The most important deletion was a passage blaming the king for the slave trade, removed to satisfy delegates from South Carolina and Georgia. Jefferson, who enslaved more than 600 people in his lifetime, sulked at the changes.

The engrossed parchment was signed by most delegates on 2 August. Its promise of equality was soon claimed by people it had left out: abolitionists, women at Seneca Falls in 1848, and Abraham Lincoln at Gettysburg.
story.zh:
1776年6月，大陆会议任命五人起草宣言，他们把任务交给33岁的托马斯·杰斐逊；他在市场街的租屋里用了大约两周写成初稿，约翰·亚当斯和本杰明·富兰克林作了少量修改。宣言开篇阐述了“政府须经被治理者同意”的理论，但正文大部分是对乔治三世的控诉清单。

大陆会议于7月2日表决独立（亚当斯预言这一天将被永远纪念），随后用两天时间修改杰斐逊的草稿，删去了约四分之一。最重要的删节是一段把奴隶贸易归罪于国王的文字，这是为了迁就南卡罗来纳和佐治亚的代表。一生奴役过六百多人的杰斐逊对这些改动颇为不快。

誊写在羊皮纸上的正本于8月2日由多数代表签署。宣言中的平等承诺很快被它所遗漏的人们所援引：废奴主义者、1848年塞尼卡福尔斯的妇女，以及在葛底斯堡演讲的亚伯拉罕·林肯。

summary.en: General John Burgoyne's invasion from Canada down the Hudson valley was stopped by Horatio Gates's American army at Freeman's Farm and Bemis Heights; surrounded, Burgoyne surrendered some 6,000 men on 17 October 1777. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States.
summary.zh: 约翰·伯戈因将军从加拿大沿哈德逊河谷南侵，在弗里曼农场和贝米斯高地被霍雷肖·盖茨率领的美军阻截；陷入重围的伯戈因于1777年10月17日率约6000人投降。这场胜利促使法国与美国结盟。

sources.title: Britannica: Battles of Saratoga
National Park Service: Saratoga National Historical Park
Richard M. Ketchum, Saratoga: Turning Point of America's Revolutionary War (1997)

summary.en: A Franco-American army under Washington and Rochambeau, with a French fleet under de Grasse blocking the Chesapeake, besieged Lord Cornwallis at Yorktown, Virginia. His surrender of about 8,000 men on 19 October 1781 effectively ended major fighting in the war.
summary.zh: 华盛顿和罗尚博率领的法美联军在德格拉斯指挥的法国舰队封锁切萨皮克湾的配合下，把康沃利斯勋爵围困在弗吉尼亚的约克镇。1781年10月19日，他率约8000人投降，独立战争的主要战事实际上就此结束。

sources.title: Britannica: Siege of Yorktown
National Park Service: Yorktown Battlefield
Nathaniel Philbrick, In the Hurricane's Eye: The Genius of George Washington and the Victory at Yorktown (2018)

story.en:
In the summer of 1781 Washington wanted to attack New York, but news that Admiral de Grasse would bring a French fleet from the Caribbean to the Chesapeake changed everything. Leaving a screen to fool the British in New York, Washington and Rochambeau marched about 7,000 men some 700 kilometres south. On 5 September de Grasse beat off a British fleet at the Battle of the Capes, sealing Cornwallis in.

The allies opened trenches and their artillery pounded the town. On the night of 14 October French and American columns stormed two key redoubts with bayonets, the American assault led by Alexander Hamilton. A storm wrecked Cornwallis's last attempt to escape across the York River.

On 19 October the British marched out between lines of French and Americans. Cornwallis, pleading illness, sent his deputy, Charles O'Hara, who tried to hand his sword to Rochambeau and was redirected to Washington's own deputy, Benjamin Lincoln. When the news reached London, Prime Minister Lord North is said to have exclaimed that it was all over.
story.zh:
1781年夏，华盛顿本想进攻纽约，但德格拉斯海军上将将率法国舰队从加勒比海驶往切萨皮克湾的消息改变了一切。华盛顿和罗尚博留下一支部队迷惑纽约的英军，率约7000人南下约700公里。9月5日，德格拉斯在切萨皮克海角之战中击退英国舰队，封死了康沃利斯的退路。

联军挖掘堑壕，用火炮猛轰城镇。10月14日夜，法美两路纵队以刺刀攻占两座关键棱堡，美军一路由亚历山大·汉密尔顿率领。一场风暴挫败了康沃利斯渡约克河突围的最后尝试。

10月19日，英军从法美两军夹道的行列中走出投降。康沃利斯称病，派副手查尔斯·奥哈拉代为受降；奥哈拉想把佩剑交给罗尚博，却被引向华盛顿的副手本杰明·林肯。消息传到伦敦，据说首相诺斯勋爵惊呼：一切都完了。

name.en: Loyalist exodus to British North America

summary.en: After the Revolution some 60,000 Loyalists left the United States, about half of them for Nova Scotia and the new colony of New Brunswick and others for Québec's upper St. Lawrence and Lake Ontario shores, along with about 3,000 Black Loyalists and Haudenosaunee led by Joseph Brant. They reshaped English-speaking Canada.
summary.zh: 独立战争结束后，约六万名效忠派离开美国，约一半前往新斯科舍和新设立的新不伦瑞克殖民地，其余则移居魁北克的圣劳伦斯河上游和安大略湖沿岸；同行的还有约三千名黑人效忠派，以及约瑟夫·布兰特率领的豪德诺索尼人。他们重塑了英语加拿大。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Loyalists in Canada
Maya Jasanoff, Liberty's Exiles: American Loyalists in the Revolutionary World (2011)
Book of Negroes (1783), Nova Scotia Archives

note: Estimates of Loyalist émigrés range from 60,000 to 80,000, of whom 30,000–40,000 went to British North America.

story.en:
In 1783 New York, still in British hands, was a city of refugees. Sir Guy Carleton refused to hand over formerly enslaved people who had fled to British lines on a promise of freedom, and his officers recorded about 3,000 of them in the "Book of Negroes" before shipping them north with white Loyalist families.

The largest fleet sailed in the spring of 1783 to the mouth of the Saint John River, where some 14,000 people built a tent city; within a year Britain carved out New Brunswick for them. At Shelburne, Nova Scotia, the newcomers briefly created one of the largest towns in North America. Black Loyalists founded nearby Birchtown but received poor land late or not at all, and in 1792 nearly 1,200 of them left for Sierra Leone.

Further inland, Loyalist families settled along the upper St. Lawrence and the Bay of Quinte, and Joseph Brant led Mohawk and other Haudenosaunee to the Grand River. Their demand for English law and institutions led to the creation of Upper Canada in 1791.
story.zh:
1783年仍在英军控制下的纽约是一座难民之城。盖伊·卡尔顿爵士拒绝交出那些因获自由承诺而投奔英军的前奴隶，他的军官们把其中约三千人登记在《黑人名册》中，随后与白人效忠派家庭一同用船送往北方。

规模最大的船队于1783年春驶抵圣约翰河口，约一万四千人在那里搭起帐篷城；一年之内，英国专门为他们划出了新不伦瑞克殖民地。在新斯科舍的谢尔本，新来者一度建起北美最大的城镇之一。黑人效忠派在附近建立了伯奇敦，却迟迟得不到土地，或只分到贫瘠的土地；1792年近1200人离开，前往塞拉利昂。

在更远的内陆，效忠派家庭定居于圣劳伦斯河上游和昆特湾沿岸，约瑟夫·布兰特则率领莫霍克人及其他豪德诺索尼人迁到格兰德河畔。他们对英国法律和制度的要求，促成了1791年上加拿大的设立。

summary.en: Delegates meeting in Philadelphia from May to September 1787 replaced the weak Articles of Confederation with a federal constitution dividing power among Congress, a president and a supreme court. Ratified in 1788 and in force from 1789, it is the oldest written national constitution still in use.
summary.zh: 1787年5月至9月，各州代表在费城开会，以一部联邦宪法取代软弱的《邦联条例》，把权力分配给国会、总统和最高法院。宪法于1788年获批准、1789年生效，是至今仍在使用的最古老的成文国家宪法。

sources.title: National Archives (US): The Constitution of the United States
Britannica: Constitution of the United States of America
Michael J. Klarman, The Framers' Coup: The Making of the United States Constitution (2016)

note: Signed 17 September 1787; ratified by the ninth state on 21 June 1788; government began 4 March 1789.

story.en:
By 1786 the confederation of thirteen states was failing: Congress could not tax, states printed their own money, and in western Massachusetts indebted farmers led by Daniel Shays closed the courts by force. Fifty-five delegates gathered in Philadelphia in May 1787, officially to revise the Articles. Behind closed windows, in a hot summer, they wrote a new framework instead, with George Washington presiding and James Madison taking notes.

The hardest fights were between large and small states, settled by the Connecticut Compromise: a House by population, a Senate with two members per state. The question of slavery was handled by compromises that avoided the word: enslaved people counted as three-fifths of a person for representation, and the slave trade was protected until 1808.

Franklin, aged 81, remarked at the signing that he now knew the sun carved on Washington's chair was rising, not setting. Ratification was fiercely contested, and the Federalist essays were written to win New York. The first ten amendments, the Bill of Rights, followed in 1791.
story.zh:
到1786年，十三州组成的邦联已难以为继：国会无权征税，各州自行印钞，马萨诸塞西部负债的农民在丹尼尔·谢斯带领下以武力关闭法院。1787年5月，55名代表齐聚费城，名义上是修订《邦联条例》。在酷热的夏天、紧闭的窗户后面，他们干脆另起炉灶，由乔治·华盛顿主持，詹姆斯·麦迪逊做记录。

最激烈的争论发生在大州与小州之间，最终以“康涅狄格妥协”解决：众议院按人口分配议席，参议院每州两席。奴隶制问题则通过一系列避而不提“奴隶”一词的妥协处理：在分配众议员时，被奴役者按五分之三人计算，奴隶贸易受保护至1808年。

签署时，81岁的富兰克林说，他现在知道华盛顿座椅上雕刻的太阳是在升起而非落下。宪法的批准过程争议激烈，《联邦党人文集》就是为争取纽约州而写的。1791年又通过了前十条修正案，即《权利法案》。

summary.en: Napoleon, abandoning his American ambitions after the failure of his army in Saint-Domingue, sold France's vast Louisiana claim to the United States for 15 million dollars. The treaty nearly doubled the country's area, though most of the land remained in Indigenous hands.
summary.zh: 拿破仑的军队在圣多明各失利后，他放弃了美洲野心，以1500万美元把法国在路易斯安那的广袤领土主张卖给美国。这一条约使美国面积几乎翻了一番，尽管其中大部分土地仍掌握在原住民手中。

sources.title: Britannica: Louisiana Purchase
National Archives (US): Louisiana Purchase Treaty (1803)
Jon Kukla, A Wilderness So Immense: The Louisiana Purchase and the Destiny of America (2003)

note: Signed in Paris on 30 April 1803 (dated); the formal transfer at New Orleans took place on 20 December 1803.

story.en:
Jefferson only wanted New Orleans. Spain had secretly returned Louisiana to France in 1800, and the president feared Napoleon would close the Mississippi to the farmers of Kentucky and Tennessee. He sent James Monroe to Paris to join the minister Robert Livingston with authority to offer up to ten million dollars for the city and West Florida.

But Napoleon's plans had collapsed in the Caribbean, where Haitian revolutionaries and yellow fever destroyed the army he had sent to restore slavery in Saint-Domingue. With war against Britain about to resume, he needed money more than a colony. In April 1803 his finance minister, François Barbé-Marbois, astonished Livingston by offering all of Louisiana.

The Americans signed for about 15 million dollars, roughly three cents an acre. Jefferson doubted the Constitution allowed it but accepted the bargain. What the United States bought was France's claim against other European powers; the land itself was still home to the Osage, Lakota, Pawnee and many other nations, and acquiring it from them would take most of a century.
story.zh:
杰斐逊原本只想要新奥尔良。1800年西班牙秘密把路易斯安那归还法国，总统担心拿破仑会对肯塔基和田纳西的农民关闭密西西比河。他派詹姆斯·门罗赴巴黎协助公使罗伯特·利文斯顿，授权最多出价一千万美元购买该城和西佛罗里达。

然而拿破仑的计划在加勒比海已经破产：为在圣多明各恢复奴隶制而派去的军队被海地革命者和黄热病消灭殆尽。眼看与英国的战争即将重启，他更需要的是钱而不是殖民地。1803年4月，法国财政部长弗朗索瓦·巴尔贝-马布瓦提出出售整个路易斯安那，令利文斯顿大吃一惊。

美国人以约1500万美元签约，约合每英亩三美分。杰斐逊怀疑宪法是否允许这样做，但还是接受了这笔交易。美国买下的其实是法国针对其他欧洲列强的领土主张；土地本身仍是奥萨奇、拉科塔、波尼等众多民族的家园，从他们手中取得这些土地，又花去了将近一个世纪。

summary.en: Commissioned by Jefferson, Meriwether Lewis and William Clark led the Corps of Discovery up the Missouri, across the Rockies with the help of the Shoshone interpreter Sacagawea, and down the Columbia to the Pacific, mapping the land and recording hundreds of plants and animals.
summary.zh: 受杰斐逊委派，梅里韦瑟·刘易斯和威廉·克拉克率“探索军团”溯密苏里河而上，在肖肖尼族翻译萨卡加维亚的帮助下翻越落基山脉，再沿哥伦比亚河而下直抵太平洋，沿途绘制地图，记录了数百种动植物。
