sources.title: Britannica: Lewis and Clark Expedition
Gary E. Moulton (ed.), The Journals of the Lewis and Clark Expedition (University of Nebraska Press)
Stephen E. Ambrose, Undaunted Courage (1996)

story.en:
Jefferson had wanted to explore the West for twenty years. Even before the Louisiana Purchase he asked Congress for money to send his secretary, Meriwether Lewis, up the Missouri to find a water route to the Pacific. Lewis chose his old army friend William Clark as co-captain. The party of about thirty-three included soldiers, French boatmen and York, a man enslaved by Clark.

They wintered among the Mandan and Hidatsa in North Dakota, where they hired the trader Toussaint Charbonneau and his young Shoshone wife Sacagawea, who carried her newborn son across the continent. The next August, at the edge of the Rockies, the captains met a Shoshone band whose chief, Cameahwait, turned out to be Sacagawea's brother; the band traded them the horses they needed to cross the mountains.

The crossing of the Bitterroots nearly starved them, and the Nez Perce fed and sheltered them. They spent a wet winter at Fort Clatsop near the Columbia's mouth and returned to St. Louis in September 1806. There was no easy water route, but their journals described some 178 plants and 122 animals new to science.
story.zh:
杰斐逊想要探索西部已有二十年。早在路易斯安那购地之前，他就向国会申请经费，派他的秘书梅里韦瑟·刘易斯溯密苏里河而上，寻找通往太平洋的水路。刘易斯选了军中老友威廉·克拉克担任共同队长。约三十三人的队伍中有士兵、法裔船夫，还有被克拉克奴役的约克。

他们在北达科他的曼丹人和希达察人中间过冬，雇用了商人图森·夏博诺和他年轻的肖肖尼族妻子萨卡加维亚；她背着刚出生的儿子横越了整个大陆。次年8月，在落基山边缘，队长们遇到一个肖肖尼部落，其酋长卡梅瓦伊特竟是萨卡加维亚的哥哥；该部落把翻山所需的马匹换给了他们。

翻越比特鲁特山时他们几乎饿死，是内兹珀斯人给了他们食物和栖身之所。他们在哥伦比亚河口附近的克拉特索普堡度过了一个阴雨连绵的冬天，于1806年9月返回圣路易斯。他们没有找到便捷的水路，但他们的日志记录了约178种植物和122种动物，均为科学界首次描述。

summary.en: Angered by British seizure of American sailors, trade restrictions and support for Indigenous resistance, the United States declared war and invaded Canada. British regulars, Canadian militia and First Nations under Tecumseh repelled the invasions; the British burned Washington in 1814; the Treaty of Ghent restored the pre-war borders.
summary.zh: 因英国强征美国水手、限制贸易并支持原住民的抵抗，美国宣战并入侵加拿大。英国正规军、加拿大民兵和特库姆塞领导的原住民击退了入侵；1814年英军焚烧华盛顿；《根特条约》恢复了战前边界。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: War of 1812
Britannica: War of 1812
Alan Taylor, The Civil War of 1812: American Citizens, British Subjects, Irish Rebels, and Indian Allies (2010)

story.en:
Many in Congress expected the conquest of Canada to be, in Jefferson's phrase, a mere matter of marching. Instead the first American invasions collapsed. In August 1812 General Isaac Brock and Tecumseh bluffed General William Hull into surrendering Detroit without a fight; that October Brock was killed leading a charge at Queenston Heights, but the invaders were driven back across the Niagara.

The Americans did better in 1813. They burned the parliament buildings at York, the capital of Upper Canada, won control of Lake Erie and killed Tecumseh at the Thames, breaking the Indigenous confederacy. In 1814, with Napoleon defeated, Britain sent veterans across the Atlantic; they burned the Capitol and the President's House in Washington in revenge for York, but were repulsed at Baltimore, where Francis Scott Key watched the bombardment of Fort McHenry and wrote the verses that became the US national anthem.

The Treaty of Ghent, signed on Christmas Eve 1814, changed no borders. Andrew Jackson's victory at New Orleans came two weeks later. Both nations claimed success; the clear losers were the Indigenous nations, who lost their British ally.
story.zh:
国会中许多人认为，征服加拿大不过是杰斐逊所说的“行军而已”。然而美军最初的几次入侵都失败了。1812年8月，艾萨克·布罗克将军与特库姆塞虚张声势，迫使威廉·赫尔将军不战而交出底特律；同年10月，布罗克在昆斯顿高地率部冲锋时阵亡，但入侵者还是被赶回了尼亚加拉河对岸。

1813年美军战绩较好：他们焚烧了上加拿大首府约克的议会大楼，夺得伊利湖控制权，并在泰晤士河战役中击毙特库姆塞，瓦解了原住民联盟。1814年拿破仑战败后，英国把老兵调过大西洋；为报复约克之役，他们焚烧了华盛顿的国会大厦和总统官邸，却在巴尔的摩被击退。弗朗西斯·斯科特·基在那里目睹了麦克亨利堡遭受炮击，写下了后来成为美国国歌的诗句。

1814年平安夜签署的《根特条约》没有改变任何边界。两周后，安德鲁·杰克逊才在新奥尔良取胜。两国都宣称获胜；真正的输家是原住民各民族，他们失去了英国这个盟友。

name.zh: 泰晤士河战役（莫拉维安镇）

summary.en: Pursued by William Henry Harrison's army after the American naval victory on Lake Erie, British troops under Henry Procter and Tecumseh's warriors made a stand near Moraviantown, Upper Canada. The British line broke quickly; Tecumseh was killed, and his confederacy collapsed.
summary.zh: 美军赢得伊利湖海战后，威廉·亨利·哈里森的部队追击亨利·普罗克特率领的英军和特库姆塞的武士，双方在上加拿大的莫拉维安镇附近交战。英军战线很快崩溃，特库姆塞阵亡，他的联盟随之瓦解。

name.zh: 塞阔亚创制切罗基音节文字

summary.en: After about twelve years of work, the Cherokee silversmith Sequoyah, who could not read English, completed a syllabary of 86 characters for the Cherokee language. Adopted by the Cherokee Nation in 1825, it spread so fast that within a few years most Cherokee could read, and the Cherokee Phoenix newspaper began in 1828.
summary.zh: 不识英文的切罗基银匠塞阔亚经过约十二年努力，为切罗基语创制了一套包含86个字符的音节文字。1825年切罗基民族正式采用这套文字，它传播极快，几年之内大多数切罗基人都能读写；1828年《切罗基凤凰报》创刊。

sources.title: Britannica: Sequoyah
Ellen Cushman, The Cherokee Syllabary: Writing the People's Perseverance (2011)
New Georgia Encyclopedia: Sequoyah

note: Sequoyah demonstrated the syllabary in 1821; the Cherokee National Council adopted it officially in 1825.

story.en:
Sequoyah, also known as George Guess, was a silversmith and veteran of the Creek War who had watched white soldiers read and write letters, which some Cherokee called "talking leaves". He set out to give his own language such a script. He first tried a sign for every word, then realised that the language could be broken into a limited number of syllables.

Friends and relatives thought him foolish or worse; one story says his wife burned his early work. Around 1821 he proved its worth with his young daughter Ayoka: separated so they could not hear each other, she read aloud messages he had written. Cherokee leaders were won over.

The syllabary could be learned in days, and literacy spread across the Nation faster than the missionaries' schools could ever achieve. In 1828 the Cherokee Phoenix, printed in Cherokee and English at New Echota, became the first Native American newspaper. It is one of very few cases in history of one person creating a complete writing system that a whole people adopted, and it is still taught today.
story.zh:
塞阔亚又名乔治·盖斯，是一位银匠，也是克里克战争的老兵。他曾看到白人士兵读写书信，一些切罗基人称之为“会说话的叶子”。他决心为自己的语言创造这样一种文字。他起初尝试一词一符，后来意识到这种语言可以分解为数量有限的音节。

亲友们认为他愚蠢甚至中了邪；有传说称他的妻子烧掉了他早期的手稿。约1821年，他和年幼的女儿阿约卡一起证明了这套文字的价值：两人被分开、彼此听不见，女儿却能朗读出他写下的讯息。切罗基领袖们由此信服。

这套音节文字几天就能学会，读写能力在整个民族中迅速普及，速度远超传教士学校。1828年，在新埃科塔以切罗基文和英文印行的《切罗基凤凰报》，成为第一份美洲原住民报纸。由一个人创造出一整套文字并被整个民族采用，这在历史上极为罕见；这套文字至今仍在教授。

summary.en: The 584-kilometre Erie Canal linked Lake Erie at Buffalo with the Hudson River at Albany, cutting freight costs between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic by about 90 percent. It made New York City the nation's leading port and opened the Midwest to settlement.
summary.zh: 全长584公里的伊利运河把布法罗的伊利湖与奥尔巴尼的哈德逊河连接起来，使五大湖与大西洋之间的货运成本下降约九成。它使纽约市成为全国首要港口，并为中西部的开发敞开了大门。

sources.title: Britannica: Erie Canal
Peter L. Bernstein, Wedding of the Waters: The Erie Canal and the Making of a Great Nation (2005)
New York State Canal Corporation: History

note: Pinned at Lockport, where the canal climbed the Niagara Escarpment by a flight of locks.

story.en:
When Governor DeWitt Clinton pushed the canal through the New York legislature in 1817, critics called it "Clinton's Ditch". The federal government refused to help; Jefferson called the idea little short of madness. The state paid for it alone.

The builders were mostly self-taught surveyors and thousands of labourers, many of them Irish immigrants, who dug with picks, shovels, horses and new stump-pulling machines. At Lockport five pairs of locks lifted boats some 18 metres up the Niagara Escarpment.

On 26 October 1825 Clinton left Buffalo aboard the Seneca Chief. News of his departure travelled to New York City in about 90 minutes by a chain of cannons fired within earshot of each other. Nine days later, off Sandy Hook, he poured a keg of Lake Erie water into the Atlantic, the "Wedding of the Waters". Shipping costs from Buffalo to New York fell from about 100 dollars a ton to under 10, and boomtowns such as Rochester and Syracuse sprang up along the route.
story.zh:
1817年州长德威特·克林顿推动纽约州议会通过运河计划时，批评者称之为“克林顿的水沟”。联邦政府拒绝资助，杰斐逊称这一设想近乎疯狂。纽约州只得独力承担。

建造者大多是自学成才的测量员和成千上万的劳工，其中很多是爱尔兰移民，他们用镐、铲、马匹和新发明的拔树桩机器施工。在洛克波特，五对船闸把船只沿尼亚加拉断崖抬升约18米。

1825年10月26日，克林顿乘“塞内卡酋长”号从布法罗出发。启程的消息通过一串彼此听得见的炮声接力，约90分钟便传到纽约市。九天后，他在桑迪胡克外把一桶伊利湖水倒入大西洋，称为“水的婚礼”。从布法罗到纽约的运费从每吨约100美元降到不足10美元，罗切斯特、锡拉丘兹等新兴城镇沿线拔地而起。

summary.en: Under the Indian Removal Act of 1830, the United States forced the Cherokee, Muscogee (Creek), Seminole, Chickasaw and Choctaw from their southeastern homelands to Indian Territory west of the Mississippi. In the Cherokee removal of 1838–39 about 16,000 people were marched west and some 4,000 died.
summary.zh: 根据1830年《印第安人迁移法》，美国强迫切罗基、马斯科吉（克里克）、塞米诺尔、奇克索和乔克托等民族离开东南部故土，迁往密西西比河以西的“印第安领地”。在1838至1839年的切罗基迁移中，约一万六千人被押往西部，约四千人死亡。

Britannica: Trail of Tears
Theda Perdue & Michael D. Green, The Cherokee Nation and the Trail of Tears (2007)

note: Death tolls for the Cherokee removal are estimated between about 2,000 and 8,000; 4,000 is the most commonly cited figure.

story.en:
The Cherokee had done much of what the United States said "civilised" nations should do: they had a written constitution, a capital at New Echota, a bilingual newspaper and courts. When Georgia seized their land after gold was found in 1829, they sued, and in 1832 the Supreme Court under John Marshall ruled in Worcester v. Georgia that Georgia's laws had no force in Cherokee territory. President Andrew Jackson ignored the ruling.

In 1835 a small faction led by Major Ridge signed the Treaty of New Echota, exchanging the homeland for land in the West. Principal Chief John Ross gathered more than 15,000 signatures against it, but the Senate ratified it by one vote. In May 1838 federal troops and Georgia militia rounded up families at gunpoint and held them in stockades, where disease spread fast.

Most Cherokee were sent west that autumn in thirteen overland detachments, through Tennessee, Kentucky, Illinois and Missouri in a bitter winter. About a quarter of them died in camps and on the road. In Cherokee the journey is remembered as the trail where they cried.
story.zh:
切罗基人已经做到了美国所说的“文明”民族应做的许多事：他们有成文宪法、位于新埃科塔的首府、双语报纸和法院。1829年发现黄金后佐治亚州强占他们的土地，他们诉诸法律；1832年，约翰·马歇尔主持的最高法院在“伍斯特诉佐治亚州案”中裁定佐治亚州法律在切罗基领土上无效。安德鲁·杰克逊总统对这一裁决置之不理。

1835年，以梅杰·里奇为首的一小派人签署了《新埃科塔条约》，以故土换取西部土地。大酋长约翰·罗斯征集了一万五千多个反对签名，但参议院仍以一票之差批准了条约。1838年5月，联邦军队和佐治亚民兵用枪逼迫一家家人离开，关进栅栏营地，疾病在那里迅速蔓延。

当年秋天，大部分切罗基人被分成十三支队伍从陆路西迁，在严冬中穿过田纳西、肯塔基、伊利诺伊和密苏里。约四分之一的人死在营地和途中。在切罗基语中，这段旅程被称为“我们哭泣的路”。

name.zh: 得克萨斯革命与阿拉莫之战

summary.en: Anglo-American settlers and Tejanos in Mexican Texas rebelled against Antonio López de Santa Anna's centralist government. After the fall of the Alamo and the massacre at Goliad, Sam Houston's army routed Santa Anna at San Jacinto on 21 April 1836, creating the Republic of Texas.
summary.zh: 墨西哥得克萨斯的英裔美国移民和得克萨斯墨西哥裔居民反抗安东尼奥·洛佩斯·德·圣安纳的中央集权政府。阿拉莫陷落、戈利亚德发生屠杀之后，萨姆·休斯敦的军队于1836年4月21日在圣哈辛托击溃圣安纳，得克萨斯共和国由此建立。

sources.title: Britannica: Texas Revolution
Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas: Texas Revolution
H. W. Brands, Lone Star Nation (2004)

story.en:
Mexico had invited American settlers into Texas in the 1820s, hoping they would develop the frontier and buffer it against Comanche raids. By 1835 they outnumbered Tejanos many times over, chafed at Mexico's abolition of slavery and its new restrictions, and joined liberal Mexicans in opposing Santa Anna's suspension of the federal constitution.

Santa Anna marched north himself. In San Antonio some 200 defenders held the old mission of the Alamo for thirteen days; at dawn on 6 March 1836 his troops stormed the walls and killed almost all of them, including James Bowie and Davy Crockett. Weeks later, on his orders, about 340 prisoners were shot at Goliad. Meanwhile delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos declared independence.

Sam Houston retreated east for six weeks, then surprised Santa Anna's camp at San Jacinto during the afternoon siesta, crying "Remember the Alamo!" The battle lasted about eighteen minutes. The captured Santa Anna signed treaties recognising Texas, which Mexico's congress repudiated; the dispute led to war with the United States a decade later.
story.zh:
19世纪20年代，墨西哥邀请美国移民进入得克萨斯，希望他们开发边疆，并充当抵御科曼奇人袭击的屏障。到1835年，移民人数已是当地墨西哥裔的许多倍，他们不满墨西哥废除奴隶制和新的限制措施，并与墨西哥自由派一起反对圣安纳中止联邦宪法。

圣安纳亲自率军北上。在圣安东尼奥，约200名守军在旧传教站阿拉莫坚守了十三天；1836年3月6日黎明，他的部队攻破城墙，几乎杀光了守军，包括詹姆斯·鲍伊和戴维·克罗克特。几周后，约340名俘虏在戈利亚德奉他的命令被枪决。与此同时，各地代表在布拉索斯河畔华盛顿宣布独立。

萨姆·休斯敦向东撤退了六周，随后趁午休时分奇袭圣哈辛托的圣安纳营地，高呼“记住阿拉莫！”战斗只持续了约十八分钟。被俘的圣安纳签署了承认得克萨斯独立的条约，但墨西哥国会拒不承认；这一争端在十年后引发了美墨战争。

summary.en: From the early 1840s until the transcontinental railroad, some 300,000–400,000 emigrants travelled by covered wagon from the Missouri River to Oregon, California and Utah. The roughly 3,200-km journey took four to six months; cholera, not attack, was the greatest killer.
summary.zh: 从19世纪40年代初到横贯大陆铁路建成，约三四十万移民乘篷车从密苏里河畔前往俄勒冈、加利福尼亚和犹他。这段约3200公里的旅程需要四到六个月；最大的杀手是霍乱，而非袭击。

sources.title: Britannica: Mexican-American War
Amy S. Greenberg, A Wicked War: Polk, Clay, Lincoln, and the 1846 U.S. Invasion of Mexico (2012)
National Park Service: Palo Alto Battlefield National Historical Park

story.en:
James K. Polk entered the White House in 1845 determined to reach the Pacific. When Mexico refused to sell California, he ordered General Zachary Taylor to the Rio Grande, land Mexico considered its own. After Mexican cavalry attacked an American patrol in April 1846, Polk told Congress that American blood had been shed on American soil. A young congressman, Abraham Lincoln, demanded to know the exact spot.

The war went the Americans' way. Taylor won at Palo Alto and Monterrey; Stephen Kearny took Santa Fe without a fight and marched on to California. In 1847 Winfield Scott landed at Veracruz and fought his way along Cortés's route to Mexico City, where young cadets died defending Chapultepec castle; Mexico remembers them as the Niños Héroes.

The treaty gave the United States California, Nevada, Utah and most of Arizona and New Mexico, for 15 million dollars. Ulysses S. Grant, who served as a lieutenant, later wrote that he counted it among the most unjust wars a strong nation had ever fought against a weak one. The question of whether slavery would spread into the conquered lands set the country on the road to civil war.
story.zh:
詹姆斯·K·波尔克1845年入主白宫时，决心让美国疆域抵达太平洋。墨西哥拒绝出售加利福尼亚后，他命令扎卡里·泰勒将军进军格兰德河，那是墨西哥视为己有的土地。1846年4月墨西哥骑兵袭击了一支美军巡逻队，波尔克随即对国会说，美国人的血洒在了美国的土地上。一位年轻的众议员亚伯拉罕·林肯要求他指出流血的确切地点。

战局对美国有利。泰勒在帕洛阿尔托和蒙特雷获胜；斯蒂芬·卡尼兵不血刃拿下圣菲，又挥师加利福尼亚。1847年温菲尔德·斯科特在韦拉克鲁斯登陆，沿当年科尔特斯的路线一路打到墨西哥城；在那里，保卫查普尔特佩克城堡的少年军校学员战死，墨西哥人尊称他们为“少年英雄”。

条约使美国以1500万美元得到加利福尼亚、内华达、犹他以及亚利桑那和新墨西哥的大部分地区。曾以中尉身份参战的尤利西斯·S·格兰特后来写道，他认为这是强国对弱国所打的最不义的战争之一。被征服的土地上是否允许奴隶制，这一问题把美国推上了内战之路。

summary.en: The first women's rights convention in the United States met in a Wesleyan chapel in Seneca Falls, New York, and adopted a Declaration of Sentiments, modelled on the Declaration of Independence. Its call for women's right to vote passed only after Frederick Douglass spoke in support.
summary.zh: 美国第一次妇女权利大会在纽约州塞尼卡福尔斯的一座卫斯理宗礼拜堂召开，通过了仿照《独立宣言》写成的《情感宣言》。要求妇女选举权的决议在弗雷德里克·道格拉斯发言支持后才获通过。

sources.title: National Park Service: Women's Rights National Historical Park
Britannica: Seneca Falls Convention
Judith Wellman, The Road to Seneca Falls (2004)

story.en:
The idea was born over tea. In July 1848 Elizabeth Cady Stanton, a restless mother of three, joined the Quaker preacher Lucretia Mott and three other women for tea near Seneca Falls. Eight years earlier, at the World Anti-Slavery Convention in London, Stanton and Mott had been made to sit behind a curtain because they were women. Now they placed a notice in the local paper calling a convention for the following week.

About 300 people came on 19 and 20 July. Stanton's Declaration of Sentiments began by echoing 1776 with one change: all men and women are created equal. It listed the wrongs of men against women, from the loss of a married woman's property to exclusion from colleges and the pulpit.

The resolution demanding the vote shocked even some supporters; Mott feared it would make them ridiculous. Frederick Douglass, the only African American present, rose to argue that the world would be better if women shared in government, and it narrowly passed. Sixty-eight women and thirty-two men signed. Only one signer, Charlotte Woodward, is believed to have lived to see the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920.
story.zh:
这个想法诞生于一次茶叙。1848年7月，三个孩子的母亲、心绪难平的伊丽莎白·卡迪·斯坦顿在塞尼卡福尔斯附近与贵格会女传道人卢克丽霞·莫特和另外三位女性一起喝茶。八年前在伦敦召开的世界反奴隶制大会上，斯坦顿和莫特因为是女性而被安排坐在帘子后面。如今她们在当地报纸上刊登启事，召集下周召开大会。

7月19日和20日约有300人到会。斯坦顿起草的《情感宣言》开篇仿照1776年的宣言，只改了一处：所有男人和女人生而平等。宣言列举了男性对女性的种种不公，从已婚妇女丧失财产权到被大学和讲坛拒之门外。

要求选举权的决议甚至令一些支持者震惊，莫特担心这会让她们沦为笑柄。唯一到场的非裔美国人弗雷德里克·道格拉斯起身发言，认为女性参与治理会让世界更美好，决议才以微弱多数通过。68位女性和32位男性在宣言上签名。据信只有一位签名者夏洛特·伍德沃德活到了1920年第十九条修正案通过的那一天。

summary.en: James Marshall's discovery of gold at Sutter's sawmill in January 1848 drew some 300,000 people to California from the eastern states, Latin America, Europe, Australia and China. San Francisco grew from a village into a city, California became a state in 1850, and Native Californians suffered catastrophic violence.
summary.zh: 1848年1月詹姆斯·马歇尔在萨特锯木厂发现黄金，吸引了约三十万人从美国东部、拉丁美洲、欧洲、澳大利亚和中国涌入加利福尼亚。旧金山从村落变为城市，加利福尼亚于1850年建州，加州原住民则遭受了灾难性的暴力。

sources.title: Britannica: California Gold Rush
H. W. Brands, The Age of Gold: The California Gold Rush and the New American Dream (2002)
Benjamin Madley, An American Genocide: The United States and the California Indian Catastrophe, 1846–1873 (2016)

story.en:
On 24 January 1848 James Marshall, a carpenter building a sawmill for the Swiss-born rancher John Sutter on the American River, saw flakes shining in the tailrace. Sutter tried to keep the find quiet; within weeks the San Francisco merchant Samuel Brannan walked the streets waving a bottle of gold dust. In December President Polk confirmed the news to Congress.

The forty-niners came by three routes: around Cape Horn, across the Isthmus of Panama, or overland by wagon. Ships in San Francisco Bay were abandoned as crews ran for the hills. The town's population went from about 1,000 to 25,000 in two years. Some 20,000 Chinese miners arrived by 1852, calling California Gam Saan, Gold Mountain; the state soon taxed foreign miners heavily.

For the Native peoples of California the rush was a disaster. Disease, starvation and massacres, many carried out by militias the state paid for, reduced their population from perhaps 150,000 in 1846 to about 30,000 by 1870. Few miners grew rich; merchants such as Levi Strauss did better.
story.zh:
1848年1月24日，木匠詹姆斯·马歇尔正在亚美利加河畔为瑞士出生的牧场主约翰·萨特修建锯木厂，他在尾水渠里看到了闪光的金屑。萨特想封锁消息，但几周之内，旧金山商人塞缪尔·布兰南就挥舞着一瓶金沙走上街头。12月，波尔克总统向国会证实了这一消息。

“四九人”经三条路线而来：绕道合恩角、穿越巴拿马地峡，或乘篷车走陆路。旧金山湾里的船只被弃置，船员纷纷跑进山里。两年间，该镇人口从约1000人激增至25000人。到1852年，约有两万名中国矿工抵达，他们称加利福尼亚为“金山”；州政府很快对外国矿工征收重税。

对加利福尼亚原住民而言，淘金热是一场灾难。疾病、饥饿和屠杀（其中许多由州政府出资的民兵实施）使他们的人口从1846年的约十五万锐减到1870年的约三万。真正发财的矿工寥寥无几，倒是李维·斯特劳斯这样的商人赚得更多。

summary.en: Eleven slaveholding Southern states seceded after Abraham Lincoln's election and formed the Confederate States of America. Four years of war, the deadliest in American history with about 620,000–750,000 dead, ended with Union victory, the preservation of the United States and the abolition of slavery.
summary.zh: 亚伯拉罕·林肯当选后，南方十一个蓄奴州脱离联邦，组成美利坚联盟国。四年战争是美国历史上最惨烈的战争，死亡约62万至75万人，最终以联邦胜利告终，美国得以保全，奴隶制被废除。

James M. McPherson, Battle Cry of Freedom: The Civil War Era (1988)
J. David Hacker, "A Census-Based Count of the Civil War Dead", Civil War History 57 (2011)

note: The traditional death toll of about 620,000 was revised upward to around 750,000 by Hacker (2011).

story.en:
Lincoln won the presidency in November 1860 without a single electoral vote from the South, on a platform of stopping slavery's spread into the western territories. Seven states of the Deep South seceded before he took office, declaring slavery the cornerstone of their new Confederacy. When Confederate guns opened on Fort Sumter in Charleston harbour in April 1861 and Lincoln called for troops, four more states joined them.

Both sides expected a short war. Instead armies of hundreds of thousands, using rifled muskets and railways, fought battles of unprecedented slaughter: at Antietam in September 1862 about 23,000 men were killed or wounded in a day. In the West, Ulysses S. Grant took Vicksburg in July 1863 and split the Confederacy along the Mississippi, the same week that Robert E. Lee's invasion of the North failed at Gettysburg.

The war changed its purpose as it went. With the Emancipation Proclamation of 1863, and as nearly 200,000 Black soldiers and sailors joined the Union forces, it became a war against slavery. Lee surrendered at Appomattox on 9 April 1865; five days later Lincoln was assassinated in Washington.
story.zh:
1860年11月，林肯以阻止奴隶制向西部领地扩展的纲领赢得总统大选，在南方没有得到一张选举人票。他就职前，南方腹地七个州便已宣布脱离联邦，宣称奴隶制是其新联盟国的基石。1861年4月，联盟国的大炮轰击查尔斯顿港的萨姆特堡，林肯随即征兵，又有四个州加入了南方。

双方都以为战争会很快结束。结果，数十万人的大军使用线膛枪和铁路，打出了空前惨烈的战役：1862年9月的安提塔姆一天之内约有两万三千人伤亡。在西线，尤利西斯·S·格兰特于1863年7月攻下维克斯堡，沿密西西比河把联盟国一分为二；同一周，罗伯特·E·李入侵北方的行动在葛底斯堡失败。

战争的目的在进行中发生了变化。随着1863年《解放奴隶宣言》的颁布，以及近二十万黑人士兵和水兵加入联邦军队，它变成了一场反对奴隶制的战争。1865年4月9日，李在阿波马托克斯投降；五天后，林肯在华盛顿遇刺身亡。

summary.en: Using his war powers, Lincoln declared free all enslaved people in the areas still in rebellion as of 1 January 1863 and opened the Union army to Black men. It freed few people at once but turned the war into a fight for freedom; the Thirteenth Amendment (1865) abolished slavery everywhere in the country.
summary.zh: 林肯运用战时权力宣布，截至1863年1月1日仍处于叛乱状态地区的所有被奴役者一律获得自由，并允许黑人男子加入联邦军队。宣言当时直接解放的人不多，却把战争变成了一场争取自由的斗争；1865年的第十三条修正案在全国范围废除了奴隶制。

sources.title: National Archives (US): The Emancipation Proclamation
Britannica: Emancipation Proclamation
Eric Foner, The Fiery Trial: Abraham Lincoln and American Slavery (2010)

note: The preliminary proclamation was issued on 22 September 1862; the final proclamation took effect on 1 January 1863.

story.en:
By the summer of 1862 Lincoln had decided that freeing the enslaved people of the rebel states was a military necessity: their labour fed the Confederacy, and thousands were already escaping to Union lines. His cabinet advised him to wait for a victory so it would not look like desperation. The bloody standoff at Antietam gave him one, and on 22 September he warned the South that unless it returned by New Year's Day its slaves would be "forever free".

On 1 January 1863, after shaking hands with hundreds of visitors at a White House reception, Lincoln signed the final text. His hand trembled from the handshakes, and he remarked that if his name ever went into history it would be for this act. In Boston, Frederick Douglass waited with a crowd at Tremont Temple until the news arrived by telegraph late in the evening.

The proclamation did not apply to the loyal border states, and it could only take effect where Union armies advanced. But every mile the army marched became a mile of freedom, and in Texas the news of its enforcement on 19 June 1865 is still celebrated as Juneteenth.
story.zh:
到1862年夏，林肯已认定解放叛乱各州的被奴役者是军事上的必需：他们的劳动养活着联盟国，而且已有成千上万人逃往联邦军队一方。内阁建议他等待一场胜利再发布，以免显得是孤注一掷。安提塔姆的血腥僵局给了他这个机会：9月22日，他警告南方，若到新年仍不回归，其奴隶将“永远获得自由”。

1863年1月1日，林肯在白宫招待会上与数百名来宾握手之后，签署了宣言的最终文本。握手太多让他的手在发抖，他说，如果他的名字将载入史册，那就是因为这件事。在波士顿，弗雷德里克·道格拉斯和一群人在特里蒙特会堂等候，直到深夜电报传来消息。

宣言并不适用于忠于联邦的边境州，也只有在联邦军队推进的地方才能生效。但军队每前进一英里，就有一英里土地获得自由；1865年6月19日宣言在得克萨斯得到执行，这一天至今仍作为“六月节”被纪念。

summary.en: Over three days in July 1863 the Union Army of the Potomac under George Meade defeated Robert E. Lee's invasion of Pennsylvania, ending with the failure of Pickett's Charge. With some 50,000 casualties it was the largest battle of the war; Lincoln's Gettysburg Address followed in November.
summary.zh: 1863年7月的三天里，乔治·米德指挥的联邦波托马克军团挫败了罗伯特·E·李对宾夕法尼亚的入侵，战役以“皮克特冲锋”失败告终。约五万人伤亡，是内战中规模最大的战役；同年11月林肯发表了葛底斯堡演说。

sources.title: National Park Service: Gettysburg National Military Park
Britannica: Battle of Gettysburg
Allen C. Guelzo, Gettysburg: The Last Invasion (2013)

story.en:
After his victory at Chancellorsville, Lee marched north, hoping a win on Northern soil would break the Union's will. The armies collided almost by accident at Gettysburg, a market town where ten roads met, on 1 July 1863. Confederates drove the Union troops through the streets onto Cemetery Hill and Culp's Hill, a fish-hook of high ground that Meade's army then held.

On 2 July Lee attacked both flanks. On Little Round Top a regiment from Maine under Colonel Joshua Chamberlain, out of ammunition, held the extreme left with a downhill bayonet charge. On 3 July Lee gambled on the centre: after a huge artillery barrage some 12,500 men under Generals Pickett, Pettigrew and Trimble crossed more than a kilometre of open fields. Fewer than half returned.

Lee retreated to Virginia; he never again invaded the North. In November Lincoln came to dedicate a cemetery for the Union dead. His address lasted about two minutes and recast the war as a test of whether a nation dedicated to equality could endure.
story.zh:
在钱斯勒斯维尔获胜后，李挥师北上，希望在北方土地上的一场胜利能摧毁联邦的意志。1863年7月1日，两军几乎是偶然地在十条道路交汇的集镇葛底斯堡相遇。南军把联邦部队赶过街道，退到公墓岭和卡尔普山上，这片鱼钩形的高地随后由米德的军队据守。

7月2日，李进攻两翼。在小圆顶山，约书亚·张伯伦上校率领的缅因团弹药耗尽，以一次冲下山坡的刺刀冲锋守住了联邦军的最左翼。7月3日，李把赌注押在中路：经过一轮猛烈的炮击，皮克特、佩蒂格鲁和特林布尔三位将军率约一万两千五百人穿越一公里多的开阔田野。生还者不到一半。

李撤回弗吉尼亚，此后再未入侵北方。11月，林肯前来为联邦阵亡将士墓地揭幕。他的演说只有约两分钟，却把这场战争重新诠释为一次考验：一个致力于平等的国家能否长存。

summary.en: After taking Atlanta, William T. Sherman cut loose from his supply lines and marched 62,000 Union soldiers some 460 km across Georgia to Savannah, living off the land and destroying railways, mills and plantations in a swath up to 100 km wide. Thousands of enslaved people followed the army to freedom.
summary.zh: 攻占亚特兰大后，威廉·T·谢尔曼切断补给线，率6.2万名联邦士兵穿越佐治亚约460公里直抵萨凡纳，就地征粮，在宽达百公里的地带摧毁铁路、工厂和种植园。数以千计的被奴役者追随军队走向自由。

sources.title: New Georgia Encyclopedia: Sherman's March to the Sea
Britannica: Sherman's March to the Sea
Joseph T. Glatthaar, The March to the Sea and Beyond (1985)

story.en:
Sherman had argued for weeks with Grant that his army could live off the rich farms of Georgia and that marching through the heart of the Confederacy would prove its government could not protect its people. He promised to "make Georgia howl". On 15 November 1864, with Atlanta's warehouses and rail yards burning behind them, two great columns headed southeast. For a month the North had almost no news of them.

Foraging parties, nicknamed "bummers", stripped barns and smokehouses. Soldiers heated rails over bonfires and twisted them around trees into "Sherman's neckties". Destruction was aimed mostly at property, though looting and assaults occurred, and Confederate cavalry and deserters plundered too.

Thousands of freedpeople followed the columns; at Ebenezer Creek a Union general pulled up the pontoon bridge ahead of them, and many drowned or were recaptured. On 21 December Sherman entered Savannah and telegraphed Lincoln, offering the city as a Christmas gift. In January his Special Field Orders No. 15 set aside coastal land for freed families, the origin of the phrase "forty acres and a mule".
story.zh:
谢尔曼与格兰特争论了数周，力主他的军队可以靠佐治亚富饶的农庄供养，并认为穿越联盟国腹地进军将证明其政府无力保护人民。他承诺要“让佐治亚哀嚎”。1864年11月15日，亚特兰大的仓库和铁路场站在身后燃烧，两路大军向东南进发。此后一个月，北方几乎得不到他们的任何消息。

被戏称为“流浪汉”的征粮队搜刮谷仓和熏肉房。士兵们把铁轨放在篝火上烧红，再绕在树干上拧成“谢尔曼领带”。破坏主要针对财产，但也发生了抢劫和侵害，联盟国骑兵和逃兵同样大肆劫掠。

成千上万获得自由的黑人跟随大军；在埃比尼泽溪，一名联邦将领抢先拆除了浮桥，许多人溺水身亡或被重新抓走。12月21日谢尔曼进入萨凡纳，致电林肯，把这座城市作为圣诞礼物献给他。次年1月，他发布第15号特别战地命令，把沿海土地划给获释的家庭，“四十英亩地和一头骡子”的说法即源于此。

summary.en: Under the British North America Act, the Province of Canada (divided into Ontario and Quebec), Nova Scotia and New Brunswick united on 1 July 1867 as the Dominion of Canada, with Ottawa as capital and John A. Macdonald as first prime minister. Other provinces joined later.
summary.zh: 根据《英属北美法案》，加拿大省（分为安大略和魁北克）、新斯科舍和新不伦瑞克于1867年7月1日联合组成加拿大自治领，以渥太华为首都，约翰·A·麦克唐纳任首任总理。其他省份后来陆续加入。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Confederation
Britannica: Canada: Confederation
Library and Archives Canada: Canadian Confederation

story.en:
In the 1860s the British colonies in North America were small, indebted and nervous. The Province of Canada was deadlocked between its English-speaking western half and French-speaking eastern half; the United States had just raised the largest army in the world; and Britain wanted its colonies to pay for their own defence.

In September 1864 delegates from Canada arrived uninvited at a conference in Charlottetown called to discuss a union of the Maritime colonies, and talked the Maritimers into something bigger, helped by champagne from the ship that had brought them. At Québec a month later they drafted 72 resolutions for a federation. John A. Macdonald, a hard-drinking Kingston lawyer, worked with his old rival George Brown and with George-Étienne Cartier, who won French Canadian support by securing a province of Québec with its own civil law.

Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland declined at first. The British Parliament passed the act in March 1867, and on 1 July bells and bonfires greeted the new Dominion. Within six years it had bought Rupert's Land and stretched to the Pacific.
story.zh:
19世纪60年代，英国在北美的殖民地规模小、负债重，且忧心忡忡。加拿大省陷于说英语的西部与说法语的东部之间的政治僵局；美国刚刚组建了世界上最大的军队；英国则希望殖民地自己承担防务开支。

1864年9月，加拿大代表不请自来，出席了在夏洛特敦召开的讨论沿海殖民地联合的会议，并借助载他们前来的轮船上的香槟，说服沿海诸省接受一个更宏大的方案。一个月后在魁北克，他们起草了建立联邦的72项决议。嗜酒的金斯顿律师约翰·A·麦克唐纳与昔日对手乔治·布朗以及乔治-艾蒂安·卡蒂埃携手；卡蒂埃争取到一个保留自身民法的魁北克省，从而赢得了法裔加拿大人的支持。

爱德华王子岛和纽芬兰起初拒绝加入。英国议会于1867年3月通过该法案，7月1日，钟声和篝火迎来了新的自治领。六年之内，它买下了鲁珀特地，疆域延伸到太平洋。

summary.en: Russia, short of money after the Crimean War and unable to defend its distant colony, sold Russian America to the United States for 7.2 million dollars. Secretary of State William Seward's purchase was mocked as "Seward's Folly"; the flag was transferred at Sitka on 18 October 1867.
summary.zh: 克里米亚战争后财政拮据、又无力保卫遥远殖民地的俄国，以720万美元把俄属美洲卖给美国。国务卿威廉·苏厄德的这笔交易被讥为“苏厄德的蠢事”；1867年10月18日在锡特卡举行了交接升旗仪式。

sources.title: National Archives (US): Check for the Purchase of Alaska
Britannica: Alaska Purchase
Lee A. Farrow, Seward's Folly: A New Look at the Alaska Purchase (2016)

note: The treaty was signed in Washington on 30 March 1867; the record is pinned at Sitka, where sovereignty was transferred.

story.en:
Russia's American colony had been run since 1799 by the Russian-American Company from Novo-Arkhangelsk (Sitka), harvesting sea otters with forced Aleut and Alutiiq labour. By the 1850s the otters were nearly gone, the company was losing money, and the Crimean War had shown that Britain could seize the colony at will from Canada. Tsar Alexander II's government preferred to sell it to a friendly United States.

The Russian envoy Eduard de Stoeckl and Secretary of State William Seward negotiated through the night of 29 March 1867 and signed at four in the morning. The price came to about two cents an acre. Newspapers mocked "Walrussia" and Seward's "icebox", though the Senate approved the treaty by a wide margin.

At Sitka on 18 October Russian and American soldiers lined up as the double-headed eagle came down; the flag tangled on the pole and a sailor had to climb up to free it. The Tlingit, Unangan and other Alaska Natives, who had never sold their land to Russia, were not consulted. Gold strikes in the 1890s and oil in the 1960s later vindicated the purchase.
story.zh:
俄国在美洲的殖民地自1799年起由俄美公司以新阿尔汉格尔斯克（锡特卡）为基地经营，强迫阿留申人和阿卢提克人劳作，猎取海獭。到19世纪50年代，海獭几近绝迹，公司连年亏损，而克里米亚战争表明英国可以随时从加拿大出兵夺取这块殖民地。沙皇亚历山大二世的政府宁愿把它卖给友好的美国。

1867年3月29日夜，俄国公使爱德华·德·斯特克尔与国务卿威廉·苏厄德通宵谈判，凌晨四点签约，价格约合每英亩两美分。报纸嘲笑这是“海象国”和苏厄德的“冰箱”，但参议院还是以压倒性多数批准了条约。

10月18日在锡特卡，俄美两国士兵列队，双头鹰旗缓缓降下；旗帜缠在旗杆上，一名水兵只得爬上去解开。从未把土地卖给俄国的特林吉特人、乌南甘人等阿拉斯加原住民没有被征求意见。19世纪90年代发现的金矿和20世纪60年代发现的石油后来证明了这笔交易的价值。

summary.en: After the Civil War the Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments abolished slavery, guaranteed citizenship and equal protection, and barred racial discrimination in voting. Formerly enslaved men voted and held office across the South until white-supremacist violence and the withdrawal of federal troops in 1877 ended the experiment.
summary.zh: 内战结束后，第十三、十四、十五条宪法修正案废除了奴隶制，保障公民身份和法律平等保护，并禁止在投票权上实行种族歧视。获得自由的黑人男子在南方各地投票并担任公职，直到白人至上主义暴力和1877年联邦军队撤出终结了这一尝试。

sources.title: Britannica: Reconstruction
Eric Foner, Reconstruction: America's Unfinished Revolution, 1863–1877 (1988)
National Park Service: Reconstruction Era National Historical Park

story.en:
Four million people emerged from slavery in 1865 with freedom and little else. They searched for family members sold away, founded churches and schools, and pressed for land. The Freedmen's Bureau set up hundreds of schools; colleges such as Howard and Fisk were founded within a few years.

President Andrew Johnson, a Tennessee Unionist, pardoned Confederate leaders and let Southern states pass "Black Codes" that nearly restored slavery under another name. Congress responded with military rule in the South, the Fourteenth Amendment and, in 1870, the Fifteenth. Some 2,000 Black men held public office during Reconstruction; Hiram Revels of Mississippi took the Senate seat once held by Jefferson Davis.

The backlash was ferocious. The Ku Klux Klan and later "rifle clubs" murdered Black voters and their white allies; at Colfax, Louisiana, in 1873 dozens of Black militiamen were killed after they surrendered. Northern voters tired of the effort. In the disputed election of 1876 Republicans kept the presidency for Rutherford B. Hayes by agreeing to withdraw the last federal troops, and Jim Crow segregation followed for nearly a century.
story.zh:
1865年，四百万人摆脱了奴隶身份，除了自由几乎一无所有。他们寻找被卖往他处的亲人，创办教会和学校，并要求得到土地。自由民局设立了数百所学校；霍华德大学、菲斯克大学等高校在几年内相继创立。

来自田纳西州的联邦派总统安德鲁·约翰逊赦免了联盟国领导人，听任南方各州通过“黑人法典”，几乎以另一种名义恢复了奴隶制。国会则以对南方实行军事管制、通过第十四条修正案和1870年的第十五条修正案作为回应。重建期间约有两千名黑人男子担任公职；密西西比州的海勒姆·雷维尔斯接任了杰斐逊·戴维斯曾经占据的参议院席位。

反扑极为凶猛。三K党及后来的“步枪俱乐部”杀害黑人选民及其白人盟友；1873年在路易斯安那的科尔法克斯，数十名黑人民兵在投降后被杀。北方选民对这一事业日渐厌倦。在争议重重的1876年大选中，共和党以撤出最后一批联邦军队为条件，为拉瑟福德·B·海斯保住了总统职位，此后种族隔离的“吉姆·克劳”制度延续了近一个世纪。

name.zh: 第一条横贯大陆铁路建成

summary.en: The Central Pacific, building east from Sacramento largely with Chinese labour, and the Union Pacific, building west from Omaha with Irish immigrants and Civil War veterans, met at Promontory Summit, Utah, on 10 May 1869. A journey across the continent fell from months to about a week.
summary.zh: 主要依靠华工从萨克拉门托向东修建的中央太平洋铁路，与雇用爱尔兰移民和内战老兵从奥马哈向西修建的联合太平洋铁路，于1869年5月10日在犹他州普罗蒙特里峰会合。横越大陆的旅程从数月缩短到约一周。

sources.title: National Park Service: Golden Spike National Historical Park
Britannica: Transcontinental railroad
Gordon H. Chang, Ghosts of Gold Mountain: The Epic Story of the Chinese Who Built the Transcontinental Railroad (2019)

note: Pinned at Promontory Summit, where the lines met.

story.en:
Congress chartered the railroad in 1862, in the middle of the Civil War, paying the companies in land grants and loans for every mile of track. The Central Pacific faced the granite of the Sierra Nevada. When it could not find enough workers, it hired Chinese men, at first reluctantly; by 1867 perhaps 12,000 to 15,000 Chinese made up most of its labour force. They blasted tunnels through solid rock, sometimes advancing only a few centimetres a day, and worked through winters when avalanches buried camps. In 1867 thousands struck for equal pay with white workers; the company cut off their food and broke the strike.

On the plains the Union Pacific laid track at a furious pace through the lands of the Lakota and Cheyenne, who attacked survey crews, and the companies hired hunters who helped destroy the bison herds.

At Promontory, Leland Stanford swung at the ceremonial golden spike and missed; the telegraph sent the word "Done" anyway, and cities across the country celebrated. Chinese workers were absent from the famous photograph.
story.zh:
国会在南北战争期间的1862年特许修建这条铁路，按铺轨里程向公司提供土地赠与和贷款。中央太平洋铁路要面对内华达山脉的花岗岩。招不到足够工人时，公司起初勉强雇用了华工；到1867年，约一万二千至一万五千名华工构成了劳动力的主体。他们在坚硬的岩石中爆破开凿隧道，有时一天只能推进几厘米，冬天雪崩掩埋营地也照样施工。1867年，数千名华工罢工，要求与白人工人同工同酬；公司切断他们的食物供应，瓦解了罢工。

在大平原上，联合太平洋铁路以惊人速度穿越拉科塔人和夏延人的土地铺轨，原住民袭击勘测队，而铁路公司雇用的猎人则加速了野牛群的毁灭。

在普罗蒙特里，利兰·斯坦福挥锤敲击象征性的金道钉却落了空；电报照样发出了“完工”一词，全国各地城市纷纷庆祝。那张著名的合影里没有华工的身影。

summary.en: When Canada bought Rupert's Land from the Hudson's Bay Company without consulting its inhabitants, Métis led by Louis Riel blocked the new governor, seized Upper Fort Garry and formed a provisional government. Their negotiations produced the Manitoba Act of 1870, creating Canada's fifth province.
summary.zh: 加拿大从哈德逊湾公司手中买下鲁珀特地，却未征询当地居民意见。路易·里埃尔领导的梅蒂人阻止新任总督入境，占领上加里堡并成立临时政府。他们的谈判促成了1870年《马尼托巴法》，设立加拿大第五个省。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Red River Resistance
Manitoba Historical Society: The Red River Resistance
J. M. Bumsted, The Red River Rebellion (1996)

story.en:
The Métis of Red River, descendants of fur-trade marriages between First Nations women and French or Scottish men, ran buffalo hunts, freighted goods by cart and farmed long river lots. In 1869 Canadian surveyors began laying out square townships across their fields before the transfer of the territory had even happened.

On 11 October a group of Métis led by the 24-year-old Louis Riel stood on a surveyor's chain and stopped the work. They turned back William McDougall, the would-be lieutenant governor, at the border, took Upper Fort Garry without a shot, and set up a provisional government that drew up a list of rights.

The provisional government made a fatal error in March 1870 when it executed Thomas Scott, an Orange Ontarian prisoner, inflaming Protestant Ontario. Ottawa still negotiated: the Manitoba Act guaranteed French and English, Catholic and Protestant schools, and 1.4 million acres for Métis children. But as a military expedition arrived that summer, Riel fled; he was elected to Parliament three times but could not take his seat.
story.zh:
红河的梅蒂人是毛皮贸易时代原住民女子与法裔或苏格兰裔男子通婚的后代，他们组织猎牛、用牛车运货，并在沿河的狭长地块上耕作。1869年，加拿大测量员在这片土地尚未正式移交之前，就开始在他们的田地上划分方形镇区。

10月11日，24岁的路易·里埃尔率领一群梅蒂人踩住测量链，阻止了测量。他们在边境把候任副总督威廉·麦克杜格尔挡了回去，兵不血刃地占领上加里堡，并成立临时政府，起草了一份权利清单。

1870年3月，临时政府处决了奥兰治派的安大略囚犯托马斯·斯科特，激怒了信奉新教的安大略，这是一个致命的错误。渥太华仍然进行了谈判：《马尼托巴法》保障了法语与英语、天主教与新教学校，以及给梅蒂儿童的140万英亩土地。但当年夏天军事远征队抵达时，里埃尔被迫出逃；他三次当选议员，却始终无法就任。

summary.en: Starting in a barn on the city's West Side on the night of 8 October 1871, a fire driven by strong winds through a drought-dried city of wooden buildings burned for two days, killed about 300 people and left 100,000 homeless. Chicago rebuilt rapidly in brick, stone and steel.
summary.zh: 1871年10月8日夜，大火从城西一座谷仓燃起，在强风推动下烧遍因干旱而干燥的木构城市，延烧两天，约300人丧生，十万人无家可归。芝加哥随即用砖、石和钢铁迅速重建。

sources.title: Chicago History Museum: The Great Chicago Fire and the Web of Memory
Britannica: Chicago Fire of 1871

summary.en: Between 1871 and 1921 the Crown signed eleven treaties with Cree, Ojibwe, Blackfoot, Dene and other First Nations across the Prairies and the North, opening their lands to settlement and railways in exchange for reserves, annuities, schools and hunting rights. Their meaning remains disputed.
summary.zh: 1871至1921年间，英国王室与草原和北方的克里、奥吉布瓦、黑脚、德内等原住民民族签订了十一项条约，以保留地、年金、学校和狩猎权换取开放其土地用于移民定居和修建铁路。这些条约的含义至今仍有争议。

sources.title: The Canadian Encyclopedia: Numbered Treaties
Crown–Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada: Treaty texts
J. R. Miller, Compact, Contract, Covenant: Aboriginal Treaty-Making in Canada (2009)

note: Pinned at Lower Fort Garry, where Treaty 1 was concluded in August 1871.

name.en: Red River War and the end of the Comanche Empire
name.zh: 红河战争与科曼奇帝国的终结

summary.en: After hunters slaughtered the southern bison herds, Comanche, Kiowa, Southern Cheyenne and Arapaho fighters attacked the buffalo hunters' camp at Adobe Walls in 1874. The US Army converged on the Texas Panhandle, destroyed horse herds at Palo Duro Canyon and forced the last free Comanche under Quanah Parker onto a reservation in 1875.
summary.zh: 在猎人大肆屠杀南部野牛群之后，科曼奇、基奥瓦、南夏延和阿拉帕霍武士于1874年袭击了野牛猎人在阿多比沃尔斯的营地。美军从多路合围得克萨斯狭长地带，在帕洛杜罗峡谷消灭了原住民的马群，并于1875年迫使夸纳·帕克率领的最后一批自由科曼奇人进入保留地。

sources.title: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas: Red River War
Pekka Hämäläinen, The Comanche Empire (2008)
S. C. Gwynne, Empire of the Summer Moon (2010)

story.en:
For more than a century the Comanche had been the dominant power of the southern Plains. Mounted on vast horse herds, they raided deep into Mexico, traded with New Mexico and set the terms for Spanish, Mexican and Texan neighbours alike. Their power rested on the bison, and in the early 1870s commercial hunters with long-range rifles killed millions of them for their hides, which tanneries had learned to make into leather.

In June 1874 several hundred warriors, encouraged by a young prophet, Isa-tai, who promised that bullets would not harm them, attacked the hunters' post at Adobe Walls. The hunters' long rifles held them off. The army then sent five columns into the Panhandle. In September Colonel Ranald Mackenzie's cavalry surprised camps in Palo Duro Canyon and shot more than a thousand captured horses.

Without horses or bison, families could not survive the winter. In June 1875 Quanah, son of a Comanche war leader and a captured Texan woman, led the last Quahadi band to Fort Sill. He became a rancher and the most influential Comanche leader of the reservation era.
story.zh:
一个多世纪以来，科曼奇人一直是南部大平原的霸主。他们拥有庞大的马群，深入墨西哥劫掠，与新墨西哥贸易，并为西班牙、墨西哥和得克萨斯邻居们制定规则。他们的力量建立在野牛之上；而在19世纪70年代初，持远程步枪的商业猎人为了获取皮革厂已能加工的生皮，杀死了数以百万计的野牛。

1874年6月，在年轻先知伊萨泰“子弹伤不了你们”的许诺鼓舞下，数百名武士袭击了阿多比沃尔斯的猎人据点，但猎人的远程步枪击退了他们。军队随后派出五路纵队进入狭长地带。9月，拉纳尔德·麦肯齐上校的骑兵在帕洛杜罗峡谷突袭营地，射杀了一千多匹缴获的马。

没有了马和野牛，家庭无法熬过冬天。1875年6月，科曼奇战争首领与一名被掳的得克萨斯女子所生的儿子夸纳，率最后一支夸哈迪部落来到希尔堡。他后来成为牧场主，也是保留地时代最有影响力的科曼奇领袖。

summary.en: Alexander Graham Bell, a Scottish-born teacher of the deaf working in Boston, received a US patent for the telephone on 7 March 1876 and three days later transmitted intelligible speech to his assistant Thomas Watson. That summer he made long-distance test calls near his family home in Brantford, Ontario.
summary.zh: 出生于苏格兰、在波士顿从事聋人教育的亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔于1876年3月7日获得美国电话专利，三天后把清晰可辨的话语传给了助手托马斯·沃森。同年夏天，他在安大略省布兰特福德的家宅附近进行了远距离通话试验。

summary.en: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors defending a large encampment on the Little Bighorn River in Montana defeated the US 7th Cavalry. Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer and all 210 or so men under his immediate command were killed. Within a year the army had forced most of the bands onto reservations.
summary.zh: 拉科塔、北夏延和阿拉帕霍武士保卫蒙大拿小大角河畔的一处大营地，击败了美国第七骑兵团。乔治·阿姆斯特朗·卡斯特中校及其直接指挥的约210人全部阵亡。不到一年，军队就迫使大多数部落进入了保留地。

story.en:
The Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868 had promised the Black Hills to the Lakota for ever. In 1874 an army expedition led by Custer announced gold there, miners flooded in, and the government ordered all Lakota bands to report to the agencies by the end of January 1876 or be treated as hostile. Many refused and gathered around the Hunkpapa holy man Sitting Bull. At a Sun Dance that June he had a vision of soldiers falling upside down into the camp.

On 25 June Custer found the village, perhaps 7,000 people with some 1,500–2,000 fighting men, and attacked at once, dividing his regiment. Major Marcus Reno's charge on the south end was thrown back across the river. Custer's five companies, moving along the ridges to the north, were surrounded by warriors led by Crazy Horse, Gall and others, and wiped out within perhaps an hour. Indigenous accounts describe the fight as fast and confused, not a heroic last stand.

The nation was celebrating its centennial when the news broke. Congress took the Black Hills in 1877; in 1980 the Supreme Court ruled the seizure illegal, and the Lakota have refused the compensation.
story.zh:
1868年的《拉勒米堡条约》承诺黑山永远属于拉科塔人。1874年，卡斯特率领的军事考察队宣布在那里发现黄金，矿工蜂拥而至，政府随即命令所有拉科塔部落在1876年1月底前到管理处报到，否则以敌对者论处。许多人拒绝服从，聚集到洪克帕帕部圣人坐牛身边。当年6月的太阳舞仪式上，他看到士兵头朝下坠入营地的异象。

6月25日，卡斯特发现了这座营地——约有七千人，战士一千五百至两千名——随即分兵进攻。马库斯·雷诺少校对营地南端的冲锋被击退到河对岸。卡斯特率五个连沿北面山脊移动，被疯马、加尔等人率领的武士包围，大约一小时内全军覆没。原住民的叙述把这场战斗描述为迅速而混乱，而非英勇的“最后抵抗”。

消息传来时，美国正在庆祝建国百年。1877年国会夺走了黑山；1980年最高法院裁定这一夺取违法，而拉科塔人至今拒绝接受赔偿金。
